summary: PC Agent-E augments 312 human computer-use trajectories with alternative action decisions synthesized by Claude 3.7 Sonnet. It studies training with this combination and introduces WindowsAgentArena-V2 as an updated evaluation benchmark.

name: EVA: Evolving Semantic Adversaries for Red-Teaming GUI Agents Against Environmental Injection Attacks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces EVA, a red-teaming framework that evolves semantic payloads for GUI environmental-injection tests. It studies the contribution of semantic versus visual deception and distills discovered patterns into reusable evaluation rules.

name: MedBrowseComp: Benchmarking Medical Deep Research and Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MedBrowseComp, a benchmark of human-curated, multi-hop medical questions for agents retrieving and synthesizing facts from live knowledge bases in a computer-use setting.

name: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Web-Shepherd is a process reward model for assessing individual steps of web-navigation trajectories. It introduces a collection of 40,000 step-level preference pairs with checklists and a separate benchmark for comparing reward models, then evaluates verification during WebArena-lite navigation.

name: AutoData: A Multi-Agent System for Open Web Data Collection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AutoData, a multi-agent system that collects web datasets from a natural-language request, and Instruct2DS, a benchmark for live collection across three domains.

name: TransBench: Breaking Barriers for Transferable Graphical User Interface Agents in Dynamic Digital Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces TransBench to evaluate GUI grounding transfer across app versions, iOS, Android, Web, and functionally distinct applications.

name: ScienceBoard: Evaluating Multimodal Autonomous Agents in Realistic Scientific Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScienceBoard combines an interactive environment with professional scientific software and 169 human-curated tasks in areas including biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics. It evaluates computer-use agents on visually rich research workflows and analyzes their execution limitations.

name: XBOUND: Exploring Capability Boundaries of Device-Control Agents at the State Level
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: XBOUND evaluates GUI agents at the level of a screen state, considering multiple instructions and possible target actions within it. The study separates action matching from instruction unification and compares effects of grounding and trajectory data.

name: AdInject: Real-World Black-Box Attacks on Web Agents via Advertising Delivery
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies advertising delivery as an indirect-injection channel for web agents under a black-box threat model. AdInject evaluates how static ad content shaped by website context can redirect browser actions.

name: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RedTeamCUA combines a virtual-machine OS environment with containerized websites for controlled prompt-injection tests spanning both interfaces. Its RTC-Bench contains 864 examples and can initialize agents at injection points to separate attack susceptibility from navigation failures.

name: Agent-X: Evaluating Deep Multimodal Reasoning in Vision-Centric Agentic Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Web browsing is one of six environments, alongside non-web tasks.
summary: Introduces Agent-X, a benchmark of multi-step visual reasoning and tool use with step-level grading across six settings, including web browsing.

name: Open CaptchaWorld: A Comprehensive Web-based Platform for Testing and Benchmarking Multimodal LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: Open CaptchaWorld evaluates multimodal agents on interactive browser-based CAPTCHA puzzles. Its benchmark distinguishes task success from the depth of visual reasoning and interaction needed to complete a puzzle.

name: RiOSWorld: Benchmarking the Risk of Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces RiOSWorld, a computer-use risk benchmark separating user-originated and environmental threats. It evaluates both risky-goal intent and goal completion across web and other computer applications.

name: FormFactory: An Interactive Benchmarking Suite for Multimodal Form-Filling Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces FormFactory, an interactive web-based benchmark for agents filling online forms, with varied field formats and evaluation of instruction-to-field alignment.

name: MLA-Trust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of Multimodal LLM Agents in GUI Environments
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained paper abstract; Android setup is supported separately by the official project README.
summary: Benchmarks truthfulness, controllability, safety, and privacy of multimodal LLM agents across interactive web and mobile GUI tasks.

name: WebChoreArena: Evaluating Web Browsing Agents on Realistic Tedious Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces WebChoreArena, 532 web chores built on WebArena environments to evaluate agents’ retention of page information, calculation, and tracking across pages.

name: VPI-Bench: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces VPI-Bench, interactive web-platform variants containing visually embedded malicious instructions. It evaluates computer-use and browser-use agents under these threats and examines system-prompt defenses.

name: DeepShop: A Benchmark for Deep Research Shopping Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete official arXiv abstract.
summary: DeepShop evaluates shopping agents with evolving query complexity across product attributes, filters and sorting preferences. Its evaluation combines checks of these individual requirements with overall task success.

name: Surfer-H Meets Holo1: Cost-Efficient Web Agent Powered by Open Weights
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes Surfer-H, a web agent paired with the Holo1 vision-language model family trained on web content, synthetic examples, and agent-generated data. The work introduces WebClick for web-interface localization and evaluates browser task execution on WebVoyager.

name: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Uses an LLM judge to evaluate and filter synthetic GUI interaction trajectories for training a compact vision-language agent. OSWorld experiments assess the policy designed for local execution.

name: MiMo-VL Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding is one application within a broader multimodal model report.
summary: Reports MiMo-VL-7B-SFT and MiMo-VL-7B-RL, general vision-language models trained with staged pre-training and mixed RL, with GUI grounding evaluated on OSWorld-G.

name: macOSWorld: A Multilingual Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: macOSWorld provides 202 interactive tasks across 30 applications, with instructions and operating-system interfaces in five languages. It evaluates GUI agents on macOS workflows and includes a separate subset for deception-attack testing.

name: Deep Research Bench: Evaluating AI Web Research Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Deep Research Bench, 89 multi-step web research tasks and a frozen collection of scraped pages for evaluating search agents and their traces over time.

name: BIMgent: Towards Autonomous Building Modeling via Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: BIMgent plans software-specific workflows and executes GUI actions for building-information modeling. It evaluates multimodal building design and reconstruction tasks in professional authoring software.

name: GUIPilot: A Consistency-based Mobile GUI Testing Approach for Detecting Application-specific Bugs
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces GUIPilot, which compares mobile design mock-ups with implemented screens through widget alignment and tests expected transitions by executing inferred UI actions. It evaluates both visual inconsistencies and workflow-specific bugs.

name: MCPWorld: A Unified Benchmarking Testbed for API, GUI, and Hybrid Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. The platform or GUI evaluation setting was additionally checked in the primary full text.
summary: MCPWorld evaluates API, GUI, and hybrid computer-use agents with 201 tasks in applications whose source can be instrumented and extended with MCP support. It verifies completion from application behavior and packages the testbed in containers with GPU support.

name: GUI-Reflection: Empowering Multimodal GUI Models with Self-Reflection Behavior
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-Reflection synthesizes reflection and error-correction examples from successful trajectories and adds dedicated learning stages for these behaviors. It introduces a reflection task suite, a mobile environment for online data collection, and iterative reflection tuning.

name: EconWebArena: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Economic Tasks in Realistic Web Environments
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces EconWebArena, a curated benchmark of economic-data tasks requiring live website navigation, multimodal interpretation, and precise extraction. It evaluates visual grounding, planning, and interaction design within multistep workflows.

name: Atomic-to-Compositional Generalization for Mobile Agents with A New Benchmark and Scheduling System
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-NEXUS evaluates compositional mobile tasks in local utility apps and online Chinese and English service apps. AGENT-NEXUS decomposes those long tasks into self-contained atomic subtasks to study generalization beyond isolated screens or short action chains.

name: FormGym: Doing Paperwork with Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4).
summary: Introduces FormGym, a benchmark for filling image-only forms, and FieldFinder, a tool that helps LLMs locate where to place text on those forms.

name: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: AgentSynth composes easily generated subtasks into longer computer-use tasks and trajectories with adjustable difficulty. Its evaluation uses the number of subtasks to probe how agent success changes as task complexity grows.

name: GUI-Robust: A Comprehensive Dataset for Testing GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds GUI task data with real-world interaction anomalies and evaluates how agent behavior changes under those conditions.

name: OS-Harm: A Benchmark for Measuring Safety of Computer Use Agents
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Extends OSWorld with tasks covering user misuse, prompt injection, and model misbehavior, with assessment of both task success and safety.

name: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Introduces a finer-grained taxonomy of GUI localization errors and a logit-based Peak Sharpness Score for analyzing coordinate-prediction uncertainty. A context-aware cropping method refines the visual input without retraining the grounding model.

name: Embodied Web Agents: Bridging Physical-Digital Realms for Integrated Agent Intelligence
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The physical component is a simulation; the supported catalog connection is its functional web interaction.
summary: Introduces environments that couple 3D physical-world simulations with functional web interfaces. The accompanying benchmark evaluates tasks requiring agents to coordinate online information and physical actions across cooking, navigation and shopping scenarios.

name: OSWorld-Human: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OSWorld-Human adds human-determined trajectories to OSWorld to evaluate the efficiency of desktop computer-use agents. The study compares 16 agents and analyzes model-call latency, changes in step duration during task execution, and excess action steps.

name: Context manipulation attacks : Web agents are susceptible to corrupted memory
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies context manipulation in web agents by altering stored task representations. Evaluation on Browser-use and Agent-E examines memory-directed attacks and the implications for secure context handling.

name: Learning, Reasoning, Refinement: A Framework for Kahneman's Dual-System Intelligence in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CogniGUI combines hierarchical visual parsing of interface elements with a GRPO-based grounding agent that compares alternative interaction paths. Its ScreenSeek benchmark evaluates navigation across applications, changing interface states, and consistency between interfaces.

name: Agent-RewardBench: Towards a Unified Benchmark for Reward Modeling across Perception, Planning, and Safety in Real-World Multimodal Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Web navigation is one scenario within a benchmark spanning seven agent scenarios.
summary: Introduces Agent-RewardBench to evaluate step-level reward models for multimodal agents across perception, planning, and safety; web navigation is among its scenarios.

name: Mind2Web 2: Evaluating Agentic Search with Agent-as-a-Judge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark assesses agentic search answers and source attribution.
summary: Introduces Mind2Web 2, 130 long-horizon tasks requiring live web browsing and information synthesis, plus an Agent-as-a-Judge framework for grading answers and sources.

name: SafeMobile: Chain-level Jailbreak Detection and Automated Evaluation for Multimodal Mobile Agents
notes: The reviewed evaluation uses Android emulation and a specific MobileSafetyBench-derived setup. Its judge and score threshold are evaluator choices, and its task population is a subset of the later MobileSafetyBench corpus. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (II.B Defense objective; III Chain-level guard and GPTJudge; IV.B Evaluation setup; V.D Judge validity).
summary: Studies chain-level risk detection for mobile multimodal agents and a language-model-assisted evaluator, assessing safety interventions together with functional preservation.

name: WebArxiv: A Reproducible Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Web Agents on arXiv Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebArxiv provides 510 static-snapshot tasks with deterministic answers for scholarly browsing, including constrained paper retrieval, content extraction, and cross-paper comparison. The study also tests dynamic retrieval of interaction history to address repetitive or incomplete agent reasoning.

name: GLM-4.5V and GLM-4.1V-Thinking: Towards Versatile Multimodal Reasoning with Scalable Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v6). GUI agents are one task area in a general multimodal model evaluation.
summary: Reports the GLM-4.1V-Thinking, GLM-4.5V, and GLM-4.6V vision-language model family and curriculum-based RL training, with GUI agents among its evaluated tasks.

name: How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies compute allocation for web-agent post-training with teacher-generated supervised fine-tuning followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. It samples 1,370 training configurations and uses bootstrap analysis to examine hyperparameter sensitivity on WorkArena and MiniWoB++.

name: Mobile GUI Agents under Real-world Threats: Are We There Yet?
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces an app-content instrumentation framework and complementary interactive and static test suites for mobile GUI agents. It studies how untrusted third-party content changes task execution and state understanding.

name: A Systematization of Security Vulnerabilities in Computer Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a threat analysis with case studies.
summary: Analyzes security boundaries in computer-use agents through a risk taxonomy and concrete adversarial case studies. It links observed failures to input provenance, interface-action binding, memory, and delegation, and proposes CUA-specific evaluation principles.

name: OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates agent safety across real browser, code, filesystem, shell, and messaging tools using rule-based and model-based assessments.

name: VisualTrap: A Stealthy Backdoor Attack on GUI Agents via Visual Grounding Manipulation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies backdoors that redirect GUI visual grounding even when the task plan is correct. VisualTrap evaluates whether poisoned grounding training transfers to downstream tasks and across web, mobile, and desktop interface settings.

name: Let's Think in Two Steps: Mitigating Agreement Bias in MLLMs with Self-Grounded Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The verifier study also covers robotics, beyond web and computer-use agents.
summary: Studies agreement bias in multimodal agent verifiers across web navigation and computer use, and introduces SGV to assess trajectories using self-generated priors.

name: Machine-Readable Ads: Accessibility and Trust Patterns for AI Web Agents interacting with Online Advertisements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares DOM-based and pixel-based web agents on a cloned news site containing advertisements, consent dialogs and paywalls. The study examines how interface presentation affects ad interaction and consequential subscription choices.

name: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebGuard, a human-annotated dataset for predicting outcomes and risk levels of state-changing website actions. It provides generalization splits and evaluates specialized guardrail models.

name: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies indirect prompt injection through HTML content consumed as accessibility trees. The evaluation tests how manipulated page observations redirect browser-agent actions on real websites.

name: Screen2AX: Vision-Based Approach for Automatic macOS Accessibility Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Screen2AX, which creates hierarchical accessibility metadata from macOS screenshots, plus datasets and Screen2AX-Task for desktop-agent evaluation.

name: OS-MAP: How Far Can Computer-Using Agents Go in Breadth and Depth?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OS-MAP organizes 416 computer-use tasks across 15 applications by a five-level automation taxonomy and a hierarchy of user demands. The benchmark separates required autonomy from generalization scope to diagnose where agents struggle as task demands increase.

name: MMBench-GUI: Hierarchical Multi-Platform Evaluation Framework for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MMBench-GUI evaluates interface understanding, element grounding, task automation, and collaboration across six named desktop, mobile, and web platforms. It introduces the Efficiency-Quality Area metric for examining execution efficiency alongside task quality in online GUI automation.

name: FingerTip 20K: A Benchmark for Proactive and Personalized Mobile LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: FingerTip 20K gathers 20K human Android demonstrations from users' long-term everyday app use, with user context, to evaluate proactive task suggestion and preference-aware task execution.

name: Measuring Harmfulness of Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The misuse tasks are evaluated in a sandbox.
summary: Introduces CUAHarm, 104 computer-use misuse tasks in a sandbox with verifiable rewards, and studies whether language models can monitor unsafe agent actions.

name: NaturalGAIA: A Verifiable Benchmark and Hierarchical Framework for Long-Horizon GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: NaturalGAIA builds verifiable long-horizon GUI tasks from human interaction intents while separating causal task structure from its verbal description. Its LightManus-Jarvis framework divides dynamic planning and context management from execution based on visual and structural interface information.

name: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Multimodal Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Web-CogReasoner separates factual and conceptual web knowledge from procedural reasoning, using a structured curriculum to train a multimodal agent. Web-CogDataset and Web-CogBench support study of these capabilities alongside web-navigation evaluation.

name: Uncertainty-Aware GUI Agent: Adaptive Perception through Component Recommendation and Human-in-the-Loop Refinement
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RecAgent narrows attention to recommended UI components and requests user feedback when task intent or decisions remain uncertain. It introduces ComplexAction to evaluate specified single-step GUI actions in difficult interface scenarios.

name: VeriWeb: Verifiable Long-Chain Web Benchmark for Agentic Information-Seeking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark focuses on web information seeking and synthesis.
summary: Introduces VeriWeb, a benchmark of long-chain web information-seeking tasks with verifiable subtasks and a complete human-annotated trajectory for each task.

name: MVISU-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents for Real-World Tasks by Multi-App, Vague, Interactive, Single-App and Unethical Instructions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MVISU-Bench evaluates bilingual mobile tasks involving cross-app work, vague requests, user interaction and unethical instructions alongside ordinary single-app tasks. Its Aider prompting module is designed to clarify intent and mitigate risky execution within agent workflows.

name: OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces OdysseyBench for evaluating long-horizon workflows across office applications, plus HomerAgents to generate tasks from environment exploration and dialogue synthesis.

name: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: FineState-Bench evaluates fine-grained GUI perception and control across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces. Its Visual Diagnostic Assistant separates perception and localization contributions in controlled interaction experiments.

name: WebMall -- A Multi-Shop Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebMall provides four simulated online shops with heterogeneous product data for comparison shopping, related-product searches, and checkout tasks. It evaluates web agents with different observation formats and memory configurations in a fixed offline environment.

name: MM-BrowseComp: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Browsing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MM-BrowseComp, a benchmark for browsing agents that must use evidence from web images and videos to answer multimodal search questions.

name: You Don't Know Until You Click:Automated GUI Testing for Production-Ready Software Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RealDevWorld evaluates generated software repositories with 194 development tasks and AppEvalPilot, an agent judge that operates the resulting GUIs. The evaluation examines functional behavior, visual fidelity, and runtime responses to produce task-specific diagnostic feedback.

name: A Functionality-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents in E-commerce Domains
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Amazon-Bench generates functionality-specific web tasks from page content and interactive controls, covering operations beyond product search. Its evaluator checks task completion and unintended changes to account state, such as address or purchase settings.

name: WebMMU: A Benchmark for Multimodal Multilingual Website Understanding and Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces WebMMU, a multilingual benchmark for website visual question answering, element grounding, code editing, and mockup-to-code generation.

publication.title: DashboardQA: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Question Answering on Interactive Dashboards
publication.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2026

name: DashboardQA: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Question Answering on Interactive Dashboards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark centers on interactive dashboards from Tableau Public.
summary: Introduces DashboardQA to evaluate how vision-language GUI agents answer questions by interacting with dashboards, grounding elements, and planning actions.

name: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study also examines tool-calling agents in SHADE-Arena; CUA-SHADE-Arena is its computer-use setting.
summary: Introduces CUA-SHADE-Arena and a red-teaming workflow for testing monitors that detect covert misbehavior in computer-use agent trajectories.

name: Mind the Third Eye! Benchmarking Privacy Awareness in MLLM-powered Smartphone Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SAPA-Bench with 7,138 smartphone scenarios to evaluate whether MLLM-powered mobile agents detect and protect sensitive personal information on screen.

name: InquireMobile: Teaching VLM-based Mobile Agent to Request Human Assistance via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: InquireMobile trains mobile agents to seek human confirmation at critical decisions using staged reinforcement fine-tuning and pre-action reasoning. InquireBench evaluates safe interaction and proactive inquiry, distinguishing asking for help from completing the underlying task.

name: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces Morae, a UI agent that detects decision points and pauses for user choices using interface code and screenshots. A study with blind and low-vision participants evaluates this mixed-initiative approach on real web tasks.

name: MMSearch-Plus: Benchmarking Provenance-Aware Search for Multimodal Browsing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces MMSearch-Plus, a multimodal browsing benchmark with iterative image-text search, and an agent framework that marks and crops images for targeted retrieval.

name: KG-RAG: Enhancing GUI Agent Decision-Making via Knowledge Graph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: KG-RAG converts UI transition graphs into a searchable vector store and uses intent-guided retrieval to construct actionable navigation paths. It introduces KG-Android-Bench and KG-Harmony-Bench and evaluates transfer from mobile apps to web and desktop tasks.

name: FlashAdventure: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Solving Full Story Arcs in Diverse Adventure Games
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: FlashAdventure evaluates GUI agents on completing story arcs in 34 adventure games. It pairs an automated gameplay judge with COAST, a framework that keeps long-term clue memory to plan and complete sequential objectives.

name: Throttling Web Agents Using Reasoning Gates
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The contribution is an access-cost mechanism spanning websites and MCP servers.
summary: Introduces reasoning gates that require agents to solve generated, verifiable puzzles before receiving access to resources. The throttling approach is deployed on a custom website and MCP servers and evaluated with web agents.

name: MobileRAG: Enhancing Mobile Agent with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MobileRAG combines retrieval and memory components to support mobile tasks that need external knowledge or long action sequences. MobileRAG-Eval is introduced to study these requirements on complex real-world app tasks.

name: Are LLM Agents the New RPA? A Comparative Study with RPA Across Enterprise Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison covers three enterprise RPA challenges.
summary: Compares an agent using computer interfaces with UiPath RPA on enterprise data entry, monitoring, and document extraction, measuring speed, reliability, and development effort.

name: SparkUI-Parser: Enhancing GUI Perception with Robust Grounding and Parsing
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces SparkUI-Parser, which adds continuous coordinate decoding and a rejection mechanism for nonexistent targets to a multimodal model. It also presents ScreenParse for evaluating structural interface perception.

name: MAS-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Shortcut-Augmented Hybrid Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MAS-Bench evaluates mobile agents that combine GUI actions with APIs, deep links, and reusable scripts. Its 139 tasks across 11 apps test use of 88 predefined shortcuts as well as the ability to generate new reusable workflows.

name: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The official full paper confirms GUI/desktop interaction alongside Bash and file tools. Its abstract and body enumerate attack categories differently; no category count is promoted into this annotation.
summary: Introduces AgentSentinel, which intercepts sensitive computer-agent operations and audits them using task context together with system traces. BadComputerUse evaluates this enforcement approach across attack scenarios involving tool and computer control.

name: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies how GUI agents, people, and human-agent teams respond to manipulative interface designs. The two-phase evaluation examines failure modes and the benefits and costs of human oversight.

name: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Chameleon, an environmental-injection evaluation framework that varies webpage content and trigger context. It combines simulated page variation with attention-based optimization and tests GUI agents across realistic websites.

name: UI-S1: Advancing GUI Automation via Semi-online Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-S1 simulates multi-turn online learning over offline trajectories, using a patch module to recover divergences while retaining the model’s own outputs in context. It combines discounted future returns with step- and episode-level advantages and introduces a semi-online performance proxy.

name: See, Think, Act: Teaching Multimodal Agents to Effectively Interact with GUI by Identifying Toggles
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces a benchmark for binary GUI-toggle instructions and State-aware Reasoning, which compares the observed control state with the requested state before choosing an action. It evaluates agents on toggle tasks and broader interactive benchmarks.

name: Detecting Pipeline Failures through Fine-Grained Analysis of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a modular framework for identifying errors at intermediate stages of a web-agent pipeline. A SeeAct and Mind2Web case study examines weaknesses that are obscured by final task-success metrics.

name: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Step Rewards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces iStar, a general agentic RL method that learns implicit step rewards; WebShop is one of several interactive benchmarks used to evaluate it.

name: Benchmarking MLLM-based Web Understanding: Reasoning, Robustness and Safety
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on web interface reasoning, visual perturbation robustness, and safety-critical web understanding tasks.

name: ProRe: A Proactive Reward System for GUI Agents via Reasoner-Actor Collaboration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ProRe evaluates GUI task outcomes by having a reasoner assign targeted environment-probing tasks to specialist actors. The additional observations support reward judgments, with separate evaluation of judge accuracy and downstream agent task success.

name: RISK: A Framework for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RISK combines browser-interaction training data, a benchmark, and reinforcement fine-tuning for e-commerce risk-management workflows. Its trajectories and rewards distinguish individual actions from multi-step stateful tasks involving deeply embedded web content.

name: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-PRA evaluates GUI progress by generating task-specific criteria and actively inspecting visual evidence with tools. It tests offline judgment on OS-Critic Bench and the effects of this feedback on online mobile policies in AndroidWorld.

name: GUI-Shepherd: Reliable Process Reward and Verification for Long-Sequence GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces GUI-Shepherd, a process reward model trained on annotated GUI interactions to give step-level feedback for agent training and verification on AndroidWorld and AndroidControl.

name: Generalist Scanner Meets Specialist Locator: A Synergistic Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Robust GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GMS pairs a general vision-language scanner that proposes interface regions with a specialist locator that predicts coordinates within them. Hierarchical coarse-to-fine search coordinates the two components for GUI grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SCUBA evaluates enterprise UI navigation and CRM workflows with 300 task instances derived from Salesforce user interviews. Salesforce sandbox execution and milestone-based assessment support comparisons between zero-shot agents and agents given demonstrations.

name: Graph2Eval: Automatic Multimodal Task Generation for Agents via Knowledge Graphs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The framework also generates document-understanding tasks for RAG agents.
summary: Introduces Graph2Eval, which generates multimodal agent evaluation tasks from knowledge graphs, including multi-step web interactions in Graph2Eval-Bench.

name: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The reported contribution evaluates attack detection.
summary: Introduces WAInjectBench with a threat-model taxonomy and malicious and benign text-image datasets for web-agent prompt-injection detection. It compares detector families across explicit and less visible forms of injected content.

name: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: BLIND-ACT tests whether computer-use agents persist with ambiguous, contradictory, or infeasible goals without adequate contextual reasoning. Its OSWorld-based tasks and judged trajectories examine these behaviors and the effect of mitigation prompts.

name: Say One Thing, Do Another? Diagnosing Reasoning-Execution Gaps in VLM-Powered Mobile-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study measures reasoning and execution gaps across mobile interaction tasks.
summary: Introduces an evaluation framework for mobile GUI agents that compares actions implied by their reasoning with intended and executed actions to diagnose mismatches.

name: Scaling Agents for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Behavior Judge, which converts execution trajectories into behavior narratives and compares multiple candidate rollouts. Experiments examine this selection approach on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and AndroidWorld.

name: BrowserArena: Evaluating LLM Agents on Real-World Web Navigation Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces BrowserArena, a live-web platform for head-to-head agent comparisons on user-submitted tasks. Step-level human annotations support targeted analysis of navigation, pop-up handling and CAPTCHA-related failures.

name: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WAREX augments existing web-agent benchmarks with reliability challenges arising from unstable systems and changing or disruptive website behavior. Evaluation on WebArena, WebVoyager and REAL examines how these disturbances affect task completion.

name: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Compliance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark addresses policy compliance in web-agent trajectories.
summary: Introduces PolicyGuardBench for detecting policy violations in full web-agent trajectories and their prefixes, and trains PolicyGuard as an efficient guardrail model.

name: Understanding User Experiences of Computer Use Agents: Design Space and Opportunities for Building Agent UX Prototypes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). AgentUXlab prototypes agent experiences for a website and runs them in a browser.
summary: Maps design considerations for computer-use agent experiences and introduces AgentUXlab, a browser-based probe for prototyping and evaluating agent UX on a website.

name: Demystifying deep search: a holistic evaluation with hint-free multi-hop questions and factorised metrics
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The benchmark tests deep search on hint-free multi-hop questions in a controlled Wikipedia sandbox.
summary: Introduces WebDetective, a deep-search benchmark with a traceable Wikipedia sandbox, and EvidenceLoop, an evidence-tracking workflow for web-agent search and synthesis.

name: Your Harness is Not Secure: Benchmarking Real-world Threat of Command Line Interface Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces AdvCLI, a sandbox benchmark for evaluating whether command-line agents carry out security-relevant operating-system tasks across multiple hosts.

name: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. It also studies supervised training followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on these browser interactions.

name: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SecureWebArena with simulated interactive websites, an attack-vector taxonomy and labeled agent trajectories. Its evaluation separates failures in reasoning, behavioral traces and task outcomes across vision-language agent families.

name: SusBench: An Online Benchmark for Evaluating Dark Pattern Susceptibility of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces SusBench, an online benchmark that inserts dark-pattern designs into consumer websites for agent evaluation. A human study checks the realism of the interventions, and agent trials compare susceptibility across pattern types.

name: R-WoM: Retrieval-augmented World Model For Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: R-WoM evaluates how well world models predict nearby GUI states, align complete procedures, and recognize milestone transitions. It retrieves external tutorials to guide simulated future interactions, with experiments on subsets of OSWorld and WebArena.

name: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HackWorld for evaluating visual computer-use agents in a capture-the-flag collection of web applications. The benchmark examines interface navigation and multistep planning during vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks.

name: Detect Anything via Next Point Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI grounding is one evaluated capability of a general visual perception model.
summary: Introduces Rex-Omni, a general visual perception model trained for coordinate prediction; GUI grounding is one capability evaluated alongside detection and OCR.

name: WebAggregator: Enhancing Compositional Reasoning Capabilities of Deep Research Agent Foundation Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The work centers on research questions and evidence aggregation across websites.
summary: Introduces WebAggregator, a pipeline for synthesizing compositional questions from websites to train deep-research agents, plus the WebAggregatorQA testbed.

name: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ColorBench represents mobile tasks as graphs of states collected from real devices, providing a quasi-dynamic environment with multiple valid paths and error paths. It evaluates single-app and cross-app tasks using completion, subtask progress, and atomic diagnostics.

name: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents LiteAgent for recording web-agent interactions and TrickyArena for enabling or disabling dark patterns in controlled websites. Experiments compare how individual patterns, combined patterns and visual or HTML changes affect agent decisions.

name: AndroidControl-Curated: Revealing the True Potential of GUI Agents through Benchmark Purification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AndroidControl-Curated audits ambiguities and factual errors in AndroidControl and produces a refined evaluation dataset. The paper also studies post-training a small Magma-R1 model on a curated subset to examine the effect of data quality on GUI action assessment.

name: CUARewardBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Reward Models on Computer-using Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces CUARewardBench for evaluating outcome and process reward models on annotated computer-use trajectories, plus Unanimous Prompt Ensemble (UPE) for reward judgments.

name: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebGraphEval, which merges multiple agents' trajectories into a weighted graph of canonical actions. Structural analyses examine recurring behavior, inefficient paths and important decision points beyond a final success score.

name: SheetBrain: A Neuro-Symbolic Agent for Accurate Reasoning over Complex and Large Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SheetBrain, a spreadsheet question-answering and manipulation agent that uses a Python sandbox and Excel tools, plus the SheetBench benchmark.

name: GhostEI-Bench: Do Mobile Agents Resilience to Environmental Injection in Dynamic On-Device Environments?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The attacks are evaluated within Android emulators.
summary: Introduces GhostEI-Bench, a benchmark that injects deceptive UI events into Android emulator workflows to assess mobile agents and analyze failures from actions and screenshots.

name: Mitigating Coordinate Prediction Bias from Positional Encoding Failures
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces Vision-PE Shuffle Guidance (VPSG), a training-free correction for coordinate drift in visual models, evaluated for localization on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces MobileRisk-Live and OS-Sentinel, combining a formal verifier for system-level violations with a multimodal judge for contextual risks in mobile GUI workflows.

name: OSWorld-MCP: Benchmarking MCP Tool Invocation In Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OSWorld-MCP evaluates how agents choose between GUI operations and MCP tool calls in computer tasks. It combines generated and curated tools, with 158 manually validated tools across seven applications, to examine tool use alongside task completion.

name: GUI Knowledge Bench: Revealing the Knowledge Gap of VLMs in GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: GUI Knowledge Bench tests knowledge of widgets, interactions, and procedures across six named platforms and 292 applications to assess VLMs used for GUI tasks.

name: Measuring the Security of Mobile LLM Agents under Adversarial Prompts from Untrusted Third-Party Channels
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Measures how untrusted third-party notifications, messages, and app content can hijack mobile LLM agents into executing unauthorized cross-app actions.

name: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.

name: GUI-360$^\circ$: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Computer-Using Agents
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Collects Windows application trajectories with screenshots and action traces for grounding, screen parsing, and action prediction.

name: WebVIA: A Web-based Vision-Language Agentic Framework for Interactive and Verifiable UI-to-Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its main objective is UI code generation; the agent explores interface states to support that process.
summary: WebVIA combines a web UI exploration agent, interactive UI-to-Code generation, and validation of generated code's interactivity.

name: AUTO-Explorer: Automated Data Collection for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Auto-Explorer, an automated GUI exploration method that records software states for training-data collection. UIXplore evaluates exploration coverage, and collected data is used to fine-tune and test GUI element grounding.

name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.

name: ProBench: Benchmarking GUI Agents with Accurate Process Information
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ProBench extends mobile GUI evaluation with tasks whose correctness depends on the interaction process as well as the final state. Its ProcessProvider supplies process information for assessing agent behavior and analyzing failure modes.

name: TaskSense: Cognitive Chain Modeling and Difficulty Estimation for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its difficulty estimates are compared with user completion time and agent success on cognitively demanding tasks.
summary: Cognitive Chain estimates GUI task difficulty by extracting sequences of cognitive steps from execution traces, then uses those estimates to assess GUI agents.

name: Can We Stop Malicious AI? KILLBENCH: A Benchmark for External AI Kill Switch Feasibility
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5).
summary: KillBench evaluates external prompt-style signals intended to halt maliciously operating web agents, across harmful scenarios and agent configurations.

name: Computer-Use Agents as Judges for Generative User Interface
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: AUI-Gym evaluates generated websites by having computer-use agents attempt tasks whose executability is checked programmatically. A feedback dashboard condenses navigation histories into visual summaries that a coding agent can use to revise an interface.

name: D-GARA: A Dynamic Benchmarking Framework for GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: D-GARA evaluates Android GUI agents under runtime anomalies such as permission dialogs, battery warnings, and update prompts. Its modular environment embeds these interruptions in Android applications to study recovery and robustness.

name: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-CUBE evaluates 226 tasks ranging from individual controls to copy-paste and enterprise workflows. Interface variations, multiple resolutions, and application-state validation support diagnosis of operational reliability beyond task accuracy alone.

name: AppSelectBench: Application-Level Tool Selection Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: AppSelectBench evaluates whether computer-using agents choose the right desktop application for a task, using generated user intents and multiple evaluation protocols.

name: "Are We Done Yet?": A Vision-Based Judge for Autonomous Task Completion of Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This study tests vision-language models as task-completion judges using screenshots and instructions from 42 built-in macOS applications. It evaluates judgment accuracy on human-labeled tasks and separately studies how judge feedback affects agent task success.

name: BrowseSafe: Understanding and Preventing Prompt Injection Within AI Browser Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: BrowseSafe builds a benchmark of prompt injections in realistic HTML for browser agents and evaluates defenses against attacks that can affect agent actions.

name: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OpenApps, a configurable app ecosystem for measuring UI-agent reliability under changes in appearance and content. Its evaluation compares task success and failure behavior across many versions of the same apps.

name: MCP vs RAG vs NLWeb vs HTML: A Comparison of the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Different Agent Interfaces to the Web (Technical Report)
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison uses four simulated e-shops.
summary: Compares HTML browsing, RAG, MCP, and NLWeb interfaces for web agents performing product search, comparison, and checkout tasks in four simulated e-shops.

name: MPR-GUI: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multilingual Perception and Reasoning in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MPR-GUI evaluates GUI perception and reasoning through strictly aligned tasks in six languages. GUI-XLI adjusts non-English hidden representations toward English representations at language-sensitive layers during inference to address the measured cross-language gaps.

name: DrawingBench: Evaluating Spatial Reasoning and UI Interaction Capabilities of Large Language Models through Mouse-Based Drawing Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DrawingBench evaluates sequences of low-level mouse-based GUI actions through 250 drawing prompts and rule-based criteria. Action inspection and multi-turn external feedback support analysis of spatial reasoning, tool-state management, and refinement.

name: Chain-of-Ground: Improving GUI Grounding via Iterative Reasoning and Reference Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Chain-of-Ground uses iterative visual reasoning and reference feedback to refine GUI localization without additional training. It evaluates on ScreenSpot-Pro and introduces TPanel-UI to probe grounding on industrial control panels with visual distortions.

name: GUI Exploration Lab: Enhancing Screen Navigation in Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI Exploration Lab, a simulation engine for composing screens, interface elements, and navigation graphs. It studies how supervised learning, single-turn RL, and multiturn RL affect GUI navigation and exploration.

name: LegalWebAgent: Empowering Access to Justice via LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LegalWebAgent separates user-needs clarification, webpage browsing, and actions such as form completion or scheduling. A 15-task evaluation studies legal-service workflows relevant to Québec civil-law users, using HTML and screenshot observations.

name: Zoom in, Click out: Unlocking and Evaluating the Potential of Zooming for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ZoomClick uses repeated zooming and context adjustment to improve GUI grounding without training. The paper studies zoom depth, crop sizes, and related choices and introduces GUIZoom-Bench to evaluate how grounding models respond to zoomed views.

name: Privacy Practices of Browser Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract describes artifact release as planned.
summary: Presents a privacy evaluation framework for browser agents covering component weaknesses, website defenses, tracking, privacy-related prompts and personal-data leakage. The framework is applied to deployed browser-agent tools.

name: Using GUI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-EDA collects more than 2,000 screenshot-answer-action pairs from engineers working across five CAD tools and five physical domains. The accompanying benchmark evaluates more than 30 GUI agents on specialized electronic-design workflows.

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.

name: MobiBench: Multi-Branch, Modular Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents offline while allowing multiple valid action paths. It decomposes agent pipelines into modules to study component contributions, configurations, and performance bottlenecks.

name: MobileWorldBench: Towards Semantic World Modeling For Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates semantic world models for mobile interfaces and studies natural-language state transitions as a tool for agent planning.

name: Step-GUI Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. The report also introduces GUI-MCP for hierarchical GUI operations and local task delegation, and AndroidDaily for static-action and end-to-end mobile evaluation.

name: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

name: VenusBench-GD: A Comprehensive Multi-Platform GUI Benchmark for Diverse Grounding Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: VenusBench-GD is a bilingual, cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark organized into basic and advanced tasks. Its annotation pipeline and six-subtask taxonomy support comparisons of general multimodal models and GUI-specialized models across different grounding demands.

name: DAVE: A VLM Vision Encoder for Document Understanding and Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: DAVE trains a vision encoder for document images and web agents using self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised parsing and localization. It combines decoder-specific encoder merging with feature fusion and evaluates web localization and agent benchmarks alongside document tasks.

name: MobileWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents in Agent-User Interactive and MCP-Augmented Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces long mobile workflows that combine agent-user interaction, cross-application tasks, and MCP-based tool access.

name: AndroidLens: Long-latency Evaluation with Nested Sub-targets for Android GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AndroidLens provides 571 extended mobile tasks in Chinese and English, with multiple valid paths and preserved environmental anomalies. Its dynamic evaluation uses nested milestones and Average Task Progress to measure partial completion of long workflows.

name: SmartSnap: Proactive Evidence Seeking for Self-Verifying Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: SmartSnap trains GUI agents to collect concise screenshot evidence of task completion for an LLM judge, with experiments on mobile tasks.

publication.identity_basis: Same work: the proceedings title is the retained arXiv title without its DECEPTICON: prefix, the same three authors appear in the same order, and the publisher abstract matches the arXiv abstract, including the 700-task DECEPTICON environment (600 generated and 100 real-world tasks).
publication.notes: Publisher proceedings edition; retained separately from the arXiv snapshot. The proceedings title omits the DECEPTICON: prefix that the arXiv title carries. Volume 2026 and pages 95945-95977 are explicit publisher citation metadata.
publication.title: How Dark Patterns Manipulate Web Agents
publication.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

name: DECEPTICON: How Dark Patterns Manipulate Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its tasks comprise 600 generated and 100 real-world cases.
summary: DECEPTICON is an environment of 700 web navigation tasks that isolates dark patterns to measure how deceptive interface designs steer agent actions.

name: It's a TRAP! Task-Redirecting Agent Persuasion Benchmark for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces TRAP, which evaluates task-redirection attacks embedded in realistic web interfaces. Controlled website clones and a modular injection framework support comparisons of persuasion techniques and contextual changes across agents.

name: ShowUI-$π$: Flow-based Generative Models as GUI Dexterous Hands
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Models discrete clicks and continuous drags with flow-based action generation, and introduces drag trajectories and the ScreenDrag benchmark.

name: ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments
notes: The paper abstract and official full-text sections were reviewed. The full text supports Windows 11 virtual-machine execution, screenshot/state observations, and mouse/keyboard actions.
summary: ProSoftArena evaluates 436 professional-software tasks across six disciplines and 13 applications in a Windows 11 virtual-machine environment. Its capability hierarchy, execution-based checks, and human-in-the-loop evaluation cover precise GUI operations and multi-software workflows.

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.

name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.

name: FronTalk: Benchmarking Front-End Development as Conversational Code Generation with Multi-Modal Feedback
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Its main task is front-end code generation; web agents explore generated sites to assess and critique implementations.
summary: FronTalk benchmarks multi-turn front-end code generation from text and visual feedback; a web agent explores generated sites for evaluation and in AceCoder.

name: GUITester: Enabling GUI Agents for Exploratory Defect Discovery
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUITestBench for interactive defect discovery and GUITester, which separates task navigation from anomaly verification. Testing-oriented plans and history-based reflection help distinguish software defects from agent execution mistakes.

name: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: BEPA adapts a small set of expert GUI traces into policy-aligned guidance through trajectories reachable by the learner and a dynamically updated task cache. It evaluates this two-level approach to reinforcement learning on desktop and web benchmarks.

name: Beyond Clicking:A Step Towards Generalist GUI Grounding via Text Dragging
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The dataset and benchmark focus on dragging to select and manipulate text.
summary: GUI-Drag provides synthesized text-dragging examples, while ScreenDrag benchmarks selecting text by dragging across varied GUI contexts.

name: WebTrap Park: An Automated Platform for Systematic Security Evaluation of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces WebTrap Park, a platform that turns web-agent security risks into executable tasks and assesses concrete interactions with live pages. It compares agent frameworks without requiring modifications to their implementations.

name: ExpSeek: Self-Triggered Experience Seeking for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ExpSeek uses step-level entropy signals to decide when a web agent should request experience-based guidance. It supplies guidance tailored to the current step and evaluates the intervention across web-agent benchmarks.

name: PersonalAlign: Hierarchical Implicit Intent Alignment for Personalized GUI Agent with Long-Term User-Centric Records
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AndroidIntent to evaluate how GUI agents infer omitted preferences and recurring routines from long-term user records. Its HIM-Agent maintains hierarchical memory of preferences and routines for personalized execution and proactive suggestions.

name: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Terminal-Bench 2.0 benchmarks agents on 89 workflow-inspired tasks in computer terminal environments, with a distinct environment, human solution and verification tests for each task.

name: Mind the Gap: Action Rebinding Attacks against Android GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies action-rebinding attacks in which an Android GUI agent’s planned input is redirected to a different application during the observation–action delay. The evaluation examines cross-application execution and the consequences of treating an earlier screen as the current action target.

name: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI): Architectures, Taxonomies, and Evaluation of Large Language Model Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Web navigation and computer use are parts of a broader survey of LLM agents.
summary: Surveys LLM agent architectures, operating environments and evaluation, covering web navigation and native computer use alongside other agent domains.

name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.

name: The Behavioral Fabric of LLM-Powered GUI Agents: Human Values and Interaction Outcomes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a controlled web-task testbed for studying how stated preferences and human values influence GUI-agent decisions. It analyzes how personas alter navigation and how prominent interface cues can override the intended preference guidance.

name: EntWorld: A Holistic Environment and Benchmark for Verifiable Enterprise GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces EntWorld, an enterprise GUI benchmark built by deriving task logic from database schemas. Long workflows across enterprise domains are assessed with deterministic SQL-based state checks.

name: From Struggle to Success: Context-Aware Guidance for Screen Reader Users in Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AskEase, an on-demand assistant that combines contextual information to provide screen-reader-friendly computer-use guidance. A study with screen-reader users evaluates task completion and perceived workload while preserving human control of the interaction.

name: MalURLBench: A Benchmark Evaluating Agents' Vulnerabilities When Processing Web URLs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: MalURLBench evaluates how LLM-based web agents handle disguised malicious URLs across attack scenarios; the paper also analyzes attack factors and proposes URLGuard.

name: GAIA: A Data Flywheel System for Training GUI Test-Time Scaling Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GAIA trains a GUI action critic on positive and negative examples, then uses that critic to collect improved examples for another training round. It studies how recycling these data affects the test-time action choices of different GUI agents.

name: SwipeGen: Bridging the Execution Gap in GUI Agents via Human-like Swipe Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SwipeGen for synthesizing varied swipe trajectories and SwipeBench for assessing their execution quality. The study examines how richer control of trajectory, speed, and timing changes GUI agents’ interaction performance.

name: GUIGuard-Bench: Toward a General Evaluation for Privacy-Preserving GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUIGuard-Bench, which annotates private regions in GUI trajectories with categories, risk levels, and relevance to the user’s task. It evaluates privacy recognition and the effect of screenshot protection on offline planning and task utility.

name: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MAGNET maintains separate memories for stable interface functions and task procedures across changing layouts and workflows. It updates frequently used knowledge and evaluates adaptation in AndroidWorld and offline distribution-shift settings.

name: MobileBench-OL: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Mobile GUI Agents in Real-World Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MobileBench-OL, an online benchmark of Chinese-app tasks spanning execution, reasoning, exploration, and noisy conditions. Its automatic evaluation and reset framework supports repeated testing of mobile GUI agents in real environments.

name: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse combines exploratory and taxonomy-guided data synthesis with supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO for GUI control. The report introduces OS-Nav for offline Android and Ubuntu evaluation alongside established grounding and action-prediction benchmarks.

name: OS-Marathon: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents on Vast-Horizon, Repetitive Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces OS-Marathon to evaluate long repetitive computer-use workflows whose execution grows with the amount of input data. It studies failure accumulation under task decomposition and GraphDemo, which adapts agents using a demonstration of the recurring workflow.

name: Continual GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Continual GUI Agents defines grounding under changing application domains and screen resolutions. Its GUI-AiF training framework uses separate point- and region-alignment rewards to adapt grounding as these distributions shift.

name: CovAgent: Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
