summary: CovAgent augments Android GUI fuzzers by analyzing decompiled app code and component transitions to identify unsatisfied activation conditions. A second agent generates instrumentation that enables otherwise difficult-to-reach activities, with coverage-based evaluation.

publication.identity_basis: Same work: the same five authors in the same order, the same WebArbiter process reward model and WebPRMBench benchmark, and a publisher abstract that matches the retained arXiv v2 abstract apart from one figure. The proceedings PDF title page carries the retained arXiv title.
publication.notes: Publisher proceedings edition; retained separately from the arXiv snapshot. The landing page and its BibTeX title the paper WebArbiter: A Generative Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents, while the proceedings PDF title page and arXiv read A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model. The landing abstract reports a WebArena-Lite gain of up to 7.2 points, as arXiv v1 does; the PDF and the retained v2 report 6.4 points. Volume 2026 and pages 123661-123688 are explicit publisher citation metadata.
publication.title: WebArbiter: A Generative Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
publication.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

name: WebArbiter: A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebArbiter generates reasoned action-preference verdicts for web navigation, using reasoning distillation followed by reinforcement learning. It introduces WebPRMBench and evaluates both preference judgments and reward-guided trajectory search.

name: How do Visual Attributes Influence Web Agents? A Comprehensive Evaluation of User Interface Design Factors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces VAF, a controlled pipeline that varies webpage appearance while retaining item semantics. It measures both agent clicks and reasoning references to study which visual design factors change browsing decisions.

name: Learning with Challenges: Adaptive Difficulty-Aware Data Generation for Mobile GUI Agent Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MobileGen estimates a mobile agent’s strengths across structural and semantic task difficulty, then samples new training targets around that profile. A controllable multi-agent generator creates the corresponding instructions and GUI trajectories.

name: Agentic Reward Modeling: Verifying GUI Agent via Progressive Trajectory-Grounded Interaction
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: VAGEN verifies GUI trajectories by first extracting readily available evidence and escalating to tool-based environment probes when needed. Evaluation on OSWorld-Verified and AndroidWorld studies verification accuracy and its cost.

name: SimGym: Traffic-Grounded Browser Agents for Offline A/B Testing in E-Commerce
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported validation compares simulated results with human outcomes from UI changes on one major e-commerce platform.
summary: SimGym runs traffic-grounded synthetic buyers as browser agents to compare e-commerce storefront variants offline, using buyer profiles derived from production interactions.

name: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: SafePred uses world-model risk forecasts to guide action filtering and task replanning. Its desktop and web safety evaluations distinguish policy compliance, task success and success under the specified policy.

name: SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SafeGround, which estimates GUI-grounding uncertainty from the spatial dispersion of sampled predictions and calibrates a decision threshold before testing. It studies risk-aware selection on ScreenSpot-Pro, with statistical control scoped to the threshold’s false-discovery rate.

name: Agent Alpha: Tree Search Unifying Generation, Exploration and Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Agent Alpha uses step-level Monte Carlo tree search to reuse successful prefixes and recover from early GUI mistakes. Comparison-based evaluation and diversity-constrained expansion guide the search, with experiments on OSWorld.

name: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebSentinel identifies suspicious webpage segments and checks each against its surrounding page context to detect and locate prompt injections. Its evaluation uses both contaminated and clean webpage datasets.

name: Do Web Agents Investigate Before They Decide?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MIRAGE, a web decision benchmark where agents must actively uncover evidence that can contradict the visible context. Separate investigation, reasoning, decision, and hallucination measures diagnose failures beyond reaching the right page.

name: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MemGUI-Bench evaluates short-term retention and cross-session experience reuse in mobile GUI agents using paired tasks and repeated-attempt protocols. Its staged evaluator measures memory fidelity, learning and execution efficiency.

name: ANCHOR: Branch-Point Data Generation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ANCHOR expands verified desktop demonstrations by generating new tasks at meaningful branch points and executing their instructions. State-aware verification and action filtering refine the resulting trajectories, which are evaluated through fine-tuned agents on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.

name: Mapping the Design Space of User Experience for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Develops a taxonomy of computer-use-agent interaction design through system review and practitioner interviews. A Wizard-of-Oz study then examines how users respond to normal, erroneous, and risky web-based execution, focusing on control, explanation, prompts, and mental models.

name: When Benign Inputs Lead to Severe Harms: Eliciting Unsafe Unintended Behaviors of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: AutoElicit iteratively revises benign instructions using execution feedback to surface harmful unintended actions by computer-use agents in OS workflows.

name: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.
summary: MisActBench provides action-level labels for task alignment, while DeAction checks proposed computer-use actions and requests revisions through structured feedback. The paper separately evaluates offline detection and interactive operation in OSWorld and RedTeamCUA.

name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.

name: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs: Leveraging the Cognitive Gap for Scalable and Diverse GUI-Agent Defense
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs introduces generated interactive challenges intended to distinguish human users from GUI agents. The benchmark targets perception, memory, decisions and actions, with backend-supported challenge types designed for scalable instance generation.

name: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: MUZZLE evaluates web-agent exposure to indirect prompt injection by finding attack surfaces in agent trajectories and refining injected instructions from execution feedback.

name: A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces A11y-CUA, a dataset comparing how blind or low-vision users and sighted users perform everyday computer tasks. It contrasts those traces with agent behavior under default, keyboard-only, and magnifier conditions to identify barriers to shared control.

name: LHAW: Controllable Underspecification for Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: LHAW generates underspecified variants of long-horizon workflow tasks and uses agent trials to evaluate when missing information requires clarification.

name: See, Plan, Snap: Evaluating Multimodal GUI Agents in Scratch
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScratchWorld evaluates program construction through the Scratch interface using fine-grained drag-and-drop actions and a complementary semantic-API mode. Runtime tests assess the resulting programs, allowing analysis of the gap between program reasoning and GUI manipulation.

name: How Smart Is Your GUI Agent? A Framework for the Future of Software Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GAL is a conceptual framework.
summary: Proposes GUI Agent Autonomy Levels (GAL), a six-level framework for describing autonomy and benchmarking GUI agents that navigate web, desktop, and mobile software.

name: WebTestPilot: Agentic End-to-End Web Testing against Natural Language Specification by Inferring Oracles with Symbolized GUI Elements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebTestPilot turns natural-language requirements into web test steps with inferred preconditions and postconditions over symbolized GUI elements. A benchmark of bug-injected web applications tests whether these context-aware oracles distinguish application defects from agent mistakes.

name: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AmbiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents under four levels of instruction clarity, including tasks requiring active clarification. Its MUSE evaluator separately audits outcomes, execution quality and interaction quality to study alignment with user intent.

name: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CATTS allocates additional inference computation when an agent’s action votes show uncertainty. The paper compares voting and arbiter strategies and evaluates this selective scaling on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web and GoBrowse.

name: Scaling Web Agent Training through Automatic Data Generation and Fine-grained Evaluation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This work uses constraint-based progress evaluation to retain partially successful web trajectories for training. It introduces BookingArena for structured booking tasks and studies a distilled agent trained with the resulting data.

name: SPILLage: Agentic Oversharing on the Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Formalizes and measures natural agentic oversharing when browser agents handle private user emails and calendars across live websites.

name: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-GENESIS reconstructs applications as lightweight web environments with executable assertions for reward computation. It evaluates the cost of these training environments and transfer from synthetic interaction training to held-out real tasks.

name: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ScreenParse supplies dense annotations of UI elements, types and text in web screenshots through an automated rendering and filtering pipeline. ScreenVLM learns to output structured screen markup, and the study evaluates dense parsing and transfer to GUI grounding.

name: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AutoWebWorld turns finite-state task models into interactive websites whose actions and goal states can be checked programmatically. It generates verified trajectories for training and evaluates transfer to WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web.

name: A Trajectory-Based Safety Audit of Clawdbot (OpenClaw)
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Audits Clawdbot safety through logged action and tool-call trajectories across local execution and web-mediated workflows, using automated and human review.

name: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebWorld, an open-web simulator trained on interaction trajectories for generating agent training data and testing candidate actions. WebWorld-Bench evaluates simulated transitions, alongside downstream web-agent training experiments.

name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions.

name: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Persona2Web tests whether web agents can resolve ambiguous requests using preferences implicit in a user’s history. Its reasoning-aware evaluation compares agent architectures and history-access strategies on personalized tasks on the open web.

name: ProactiveMobile: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Boosting Proactive Intelligence on Mobile Devices
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4).
summary: ProactiveMobile benchmarks mobile agents on inferring latent user intent from device context and generating executable sequences from a pool of 63 APIs.

name: CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract describes artifact release as future work.
summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning for continual GUI learning, using policy entropy to adjust their proportions and gradient projection to limit conflicting updates. AndroidControl-CL groups applications into sequential tasks to evaluate adaptation and retention.

name: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Web-agent tasks are one of three evaluation settings for this general memory module.
summary: Introduces PlugMem, a knowledge-graph memory module for general LLM agents, evaluated on web-agent tasks alongside conversational question answering and knowledge retrieval.

name: Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies webpage injections that affect both screenshots and accessibility trees, then trains web agents through teacher imitation, supervised adversarial examples, and adversarial reinforcement learning. The evaluation tests defenses on MiniWoB++ and held-out tasks.

name: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TimeWarp tests web agents across multiple versions of the same sites, varying visual design, frontend code and workflows. TimeTraj transfers plans across versions to collect training trajectories and study robustness to interface change.

name: WebChain: A Large-Scale Human-Annotated Dataset of Real-World Web Interaction Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebChain aligns human web-interaction trajectories with visual, structural and action data for agent training. It also introduces WebChainBench and a mid-training approach that separates spatial grounding from planning.

name: Generalization in Online Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AndroidWorld-Generalization with separate tests for unseen task instances, templates, and applications. A GRPO training system combines containerized environments with asynchronous trajectory collection to study these generalization regimes.

name: OSExpert: Computer-Use Agents Learning Professional Skills via Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Uses GUI-based depth-first exploration to verify elementary software functions, assemble action primitives, and construct curricula of composed skills. OSExpert-Eval examines how the resulting procedural knowledge supports complex computer-use tasks.

name: PIRA-Bench: A Transition from Reactive GUI Agents to GUI-based Proactive Intent Recommendation Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PIRA-Bench evaluates proactive intent recommendations from noisy GUI screenshot sequences containing interleaved tasks and user context. Its PIRF baseline combines memory and state tracking to maintain multiple task threads and identify opportunities to assist.

name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.

name: SpecOps: A Fully Automated AI Agent Testing Framework in Real-World GUI Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SpecOps divides testing of GUI-based agents into test generation, environment setup, execution and validation handled by specialist agents. Its evaluation spans five real-world agents, including web applications and browser extensions, and measures execution reliability and bug discovery.

name: CUAAudit: Meta-Evaluation of Vision-Language Models as Auditors of Autonomous Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUAAudit examines vision-language models that judge computer-use task completion from an instruction and final environment state. Across macOS, Windows and Linux benchmarks, it measures accuracy, confidence calibration and disagreement between auditors.

name: You Told Me to Do It: Measuring Instructional Text-induced Private Data Leakage in LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces ReadSecBench, a README-based benchmark for measuring whether high-privilege agents follow injected instructions that leak private data; a computer-use agent is evaluated.

name: AI Planning Framework for LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a planning taxonomy and trajectory-quality metrics for web agents, supported by 794 human-labeled WebArena trajectories and a comparison of two planning styles.

name: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Adaptive VLM Routing estimates GUI-action difficulty and small-model confidence to select a model under a predicted reliability threshold. Grounding and agent-routing benchmarks assess the cost–accuracy trade-off, with prior interaction context used for warm agents.

name: Why Do LLM-based Web Agents Fail? A Hierarchical Planning Perspective
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents a hierarchical planning framework for evaluating web agents at planning, execution and replanning stages, and reports low-level execution as the main failure source.

name: GUI-CEval: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-CEval evaluates Chinese mobile GUI agents through a hierarchy of atomic abilities and application-level tasks collected on physical devices. Its diagnostics cover perception, planning, reflection, execution and post-action evaluation across a broad set of apps.

name: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This public red-teaming study evaluates indirect prompt injection that both changes agent behavior and hides the compromise from the final response. Its scenarios include computer use alongside tool calling and coding, with analyses of transfer and model-dependent vulnerability.

name: WebPII: Benchmarking Visual PII Detection for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebPII provides synthetic e-commerce screenshots with fine-grained annotations for sensitive information, including partially filled forms and transaction identifiers. It also trains WebRedact to detect visual PII as a privacy component for computer-use agents.

name: AndroTMem: From Interaction Trajectories to Anchored Memory in Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AndroTMem-Bench for Android tasks whose later actions depend on earlier UI states. Anchored State Memory retains causally linked intermediate states for subgoal-specific retrieval and evaluates them against full-history and summary-based memory.

name: ClawTrap: A MITM-Based Red-Teaming Framework for Real-World OpenClaw Security Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents a man-in-the-middle network red-teaming framework for evaluating autonomous OpenClaw agents under live traffic manipulation.

name: OS-Themis: A Scalable Critic Framework for Generalist GUI Rewards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents OS-Themis, a multi-agent critic that divides GUI trajectories into verifiable milestones and reviews their evidence before assigning an outcome. OGRBench evaluates GUI rewards across platforms, with AndroidWorld experiments examining training and trajectory filtering.

name: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: The framework separates inference-time subgoal planning from MiRA, a reinforcement-learning method that supplies milestone rewards. WebArena-Lite experiments evaluate these mechanisms for long-horizon web navigation.

name: MedSPOT: A Workflow-Aware Sequential Grounding Benchmark for Clinical GUI
notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract.
summary: Benchmarks sequential target localization in clinical software workflows, emphasizing how early mistakes affect subsequent interaction steps.

name: Ego2Web: A Web Agent Benchmark Grounded in Egocentric Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Ego2Web pairs first-person videos with online tasks that require agents to connect the user’s physical context to web actions. It also evaluates an automatic task judge against human judgments and analyzes failures in video understanding and web execution.

name: The Evolution of Tool Use in LLM Agents: From Single-Tool Call to Multi-Tool Orchestration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). GUI and mobile systems are representative application areas within a broader survey of multi-tool agents.
summary: Surveys multi-tool LLM agents across planning, training, safety, efficiency, and evaluation, including GUI and mobile systems among its application areas.

name: IntentWeave: A Progressive Entry Ladder for Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The prototype and user study are set on a single cloud website.
summary: Introduces IntentWeave, a design space and browser-extension prototype for placing web-agent assistance across browser surfaces, evaluated through a study of three entry strategies.

name: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.

name: Towards Automated Crowdsourced Testing via Personified-LLM
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces PersonaTester, a framework that gives LLM agents tester personas to vary their exploration and interaction habits during automated crowdsourced GUI testing.

name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

name: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebTestBench for end-to-end website testing, separating checklist generation from defect detection. Its WebTester baseline evaluates test coverage, detection and sustained interaction across web application categories.

name: GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.

name: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The benchmark evaluates website development by coding agents, with a GUI agent used for verification.
summary: Introduces Vision2Web, a benchmark for website development from images, spanning UI-to-code, multi-page frontend and full-stack tasks, with a GUI agent verifier and VLM-based judge.

name: Emergence WebVoyager: Toward Consistent and Transparent Evaluation of (Web) Agents in The Wild
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Audits sources of ambiguity and operational variation in WebVoyager evaluation and introduces standardized guidance for task setup, failure handling, annotation and reporting. Emergence WebVoyager applies this protocol to a web-agent evaluation.

name: PSPA-Bench: A Personalized Benchmark for Smartphone GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PSPA-Bench evaluates personalized smartphone GUI behavior using user-specific instructions and a process-aware assessment of interaction traces. Its comparison of GUI agents diagnoses weaknesses in adapting workflows and preferences.

name: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4). The subject is terminal agents using APIs; graphical web agents appear as another approach.
summary: Studies enterprise automation by terminal agents that call platform APIs, comparing their task results and cost with other agent approaches, including web agents using graphical interfaces.

name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent cross-domain VLM compression method with GUI-benchmark evaluation.
summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.

name: When Users Change Their Mind: Evaluating Interruptible Agents in Long-Horizon Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Interruptions are evaluated through synthesized scenarios in a simulation framework.
summary: Introduces InterruptBench, a WebArena-Lite-derived benchmark that tests how long-horizon web-navigation agents handle mid-task user additions, revisions, and retractions.

name: Do Phone-Use Agents Respect Your Privacy?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MyPhoneBench to verify whether phone-use agents minimize personal data disclosure when filling forms during benign mobile tasks.

name: UI-Oceanus: Scaling GUI Agents with Synthetic Environmental Dynamics
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: UI-Oceanus converts autonomous GUI exploration and execution feedback into supervision for predicting future interface states. It compares forward and inverse objectives during continual pretraining and examines downstream offline and online navigation as synthetic data scales.

name: AgentHazard: A Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces AgentHazard, a benchmark of harmful multi-step behavior by computer-use agents acting through tools, files, and execution environments.

name: The Tool Illusion: Rethinking Tool Use in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents a controlled study of higher-level tool use in web agents across tool sources, backbone models, frameworks, and evaluation benchmarks.

name: GUIDE: Interpretable GUI Agent Evaluation via Hierarchical Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUIDE evaluates GUI trajectories by segmenting them into subtasks, diagnosing each segment, and aggregating structured findings into a task verdict. It tests diagnostic judgments on e-commerce, web-agent and Android-control traces.

name: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a safety evaluation of OpenClaw and the CIK taxonomy for analyzing how changes to a personal agent's persistent state affect attacks on its local and service access.

name: Comparing Human Oversight Strategies for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares four human oversight strategies during live web-agent sessions, examining exposure to problematic actions and opportunities to intervene. The analysis identifies timing and attention problems in control handoffs and upfront plan approval.

name: IntentScore: Intent-Conditioned Action Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains IntentScore on offline desktop GUI interactions to assess candidate actions using both their state relevance and planning intent. The reward model is evaluated as an action reranker for Agent S3 on OSWorld.

name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.

name: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces VenusBench-Mobile, an online benchmark for mobile GUI agents with user-intent-driven tasks and capability annotations for analyzing agent behavior and failures.

name: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Describes a web-trajectory verifier built around structured rubrics, separate process and outcome judgments, and explicit treatment of uncontrollable failures. CUAVerifierBench supplies human labels for evaluating these choices and screenshot-based context management.

name: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebSP-Eval evaluates agents carrying out website security and privacy tasks such as preference changes and session management. A browser extension controls account and initial state across runs, enabling analysis of failures on stateful UI controls.

name: What's Missing in Screen-to-Action? Towards a UI-in-the-Loop Paradigm for Multimodal GUI Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UILoop, which inserts explicit UI-element localization, function and usage reasoning between screen observation and action. UI Comprehension-Bench evaluates these element-level capabilities with three metrics.

name: GameWorld: Towards Standardized and Verifiable Evaluation of Multimodal Game Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its computer-use interface is evaluated through games, alongside a separate semantic-action interface.
summary: Introduces GameWorld, a browser-game benchmark that evaluates multimodal agents through keyboard and mouse controls or semantic actions using outcome checks.

name: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.

name: Same Outcomes, Different Journeys: A Trace-Level Framework for Comparing Human and GUI-Agent Behavior in Production Search Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The framework is instantiated in one audio-streaming search application with 39 participants and ten tasks.
summary: Presents a trace-level framework for comparing GUI agents with people on task outcomes, queries, and interface navigation in a production audio-search application.

name: KnowU-Bench: Towards Interactive, Proactive, and Personalized Mobile Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces KnowU-Bench, an Android emulator benchmark for mobile agents that evaluates preference elicitation, proactive decisions, consent and GUI task execution.

name: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces ClawBench, 153 everyday tasks on production websites in 15 categories; an interception layer blocks each final submission so bookings, purchases and job applications are scored without side effects.

name: CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The annotation describes risk calibration without asserting an unconditional safety guarantee.
summary: Introduces CORA, which calibrates a risk model to choose between executing and abstaining from mobile GUI actions, then diagnoses rejected actions to suggest interventions. Phone-Harm provides step-level safety labels for evaluating this safeguarding process.

name: Turing Test on Screen: A Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agent Humanization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract focuses on detectability through touch dynamics and the trade-off with task utility.
summary: Introduces the Agent Humanization Benchmark (AHB) and mobile touch-dynamics data to assess whether GUI agents' interactions resemble human touch behavior.

name: Avenir-UX: Automated UX Evaluation via Simulated Human Web Interaction with GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Avenir-UX combines grounded web interaction with simulated user profiles and structured usability measures to produce evaluations of website journeys. The paper describes its architecture and use of SUS, step-wise ease questions and think-aloud traces for automated UX reporting.

name: MobiFlow: Real-World Mobile Agent Benchmarking through Trajectory Fusion
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MobiFlow, a mobile-agent evaluation framework that fuses task trajectories into a state graph for dynamic interaction with third-party apps and measures task outcomes.

name: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HealthAdminBench with GUI environments for an electronic health record, payer portals and fax handling. Expert-defined administrative tasks are decomposed into verifiable subtasks to compare local progress with end-to-end workflow completion.

name: The Blind Spot of Agent Safety: How Benign User Instructions Expose Critical Vulnerabilities in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported results concern human-crafted tasks across eight applications and two threat clusters.
summary: Introduces OS-BLIND, a computer-use agent safety benchmark for harmful outcomes arising from benign instructions and threats in task environments.

name: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents WebForge, a pipeline that plans, generates, refines and validates self-contained interactive websites. WebForge-Bench uses these environments to evaluate browser agents across domains and controlled difficulty levels.

name: CocoaBench: Evaluating Unified Digital Agents in the Wild
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces CocoaBench, a benchmark for unified digital agents on long-horizon tasks combining vision, search, and coding, including capabilities related to GUI automation.

name: ClawGUI: A Unified Framework for Training, Evaluating, and Deploying GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents ClawGUI, a shared harness for GUI-agent reinforcement learning, benchmark evaluation and deployment on mobile devices. It combines parallel virtual and physical environments, process rewards, and hybrid CLI-GUI execution with persistent memory.

name: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: WebAgentGuard separates prompt-injection detection from the operating web agent through a parallel multimodal guard. The guard is trained on synthetic visual/textual examples using reasoning-focused supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.

name: RiskWebWorld: A Realistic Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces RiskWebWorld, an interactive benchmark of e-commerce risk-management tasks for GUI agents on websites, with Gymnasium infrastructure for evaluation and agentic RL.

name: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Perturbed, which varies screenshot appearance and instruction wording independently to diagnose grounding failures. Experiments on three related model architectures examine relational instructions, browser zoom and augmentation-based fine-tuning.

name: Beyond Chat and Clicks: GUI Agents for In-Situ Assistance via Live Interface Transformation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DOMSteer translates help requests and live page context into reversible DOM changes such as control highlighting, contextual tooltips and layout reorganization. The work evaluates in-place GUI assistance with interface tests, use cases and a comparative user study.

name: FedGUI: Benchmarking Federated GUI Agents across Heterogeneous Platforms, Devices, and Operating Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces FedGUI, a federated GUI-learning benchmark built from six datasets spanning mobile, web and desktop interfaces. Its experiments separate platform, device, operating-system and data-source heterogeneity when evaluating collaborative training.

name: Zoom Consistency: A Free Confidence Signal in Multi-Step Visual Grounding Pipelines
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract describes model routing as a proof of concept and reports a small correlation with correctness.
summary: Proposes zoom consistency as a confidence signal for multistep GUI grounding and uses it to route between specialist and generalist visual grounding models.

name: StressWeb: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Web Agent Robustness under Realistic Interaction Variability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The tests use constructed, controllable web environments with clean workflows as baselines.
summary: Introduces a web-agent stress-testing benchmark with controlled changes to layouts, interaction semantics, and execution for diagnosing behavior under varied conditions.

name: HalluClear: Diagnosing, Evaluating and Mitigating Hallucinations in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HalluClear with a GUI hallucination taxonomy, expert-calibrated evaluation workflow and structured-reasoning post-training scheme. It evaluates how these components affect hallucinations, grounding and action fidelity across GUI agents.

name: Do LLMs Need to See Everything? A Benchmark and Study of Failures in LLM-driven Smartphone Automation using Screentext vs. Screenshots
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DailyDroid compares text-only and text-plus-screenshot agents on everyday Android tasks across multiple apps and difficulty levels. Its failure analysis examines accessibility, observation modality and agent/application behavior.

name: On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study examines repeated OSWorld executions to separate execution stochasticity, task-specification ambiguity and behavioral variation. Paired task-level tests show why one successful run is insufficient evidence of reliable computer use.

name: AJ-Bench: Benchmarking Agent-as-a-Judge for Environment-Aware Evaluation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AJ-Bench evaluates judge agents that actively gather evidence from search, data systems and graphical interfaces. Its annotated tasks and trajectories test information acquisition, state verification and process verification.

name: Human-Guided Harm Recovery for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports human evaluation of recovery trajectories produced by the proposed scaffold.
summary: Introduces a preference-trained reward model for guiding computer-use agents out of harmful states and BackBench, a benchmark of recovery tasks.

name: Temporal UI State Inconsistency in Desktop GUI Agents: Formalizing and Defending Against TOCTOU Attacks on Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study examines UI changes between a desktop agent’s screenshot observation and action dispatch. Its pre-execution state checks address overlay and focus manipulation, while the reported DOM-injection blind spot limits the defense’s coverage.

name: AutomationBench
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AutomationBench, a benchmark for agents coordinating business workflows across applications through REST APIs, including endpoint discovery and policy adherence.

name: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: PlayEval measures whether generated GUI applications remain logically playable, using PlayTester to execute task-oriented GUI playthroughs. PlayCoder closes the loop between repository-aware generation, interactive testing and targeted code repair.

name: VLAA-GUI: Knowing When to Stop, Recover, and Search, A Modular Framework for GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VLAA-GUI combines mandatory checks for visually supported completion, multi-tier loop recovery and on-demand workflow search. Optional coding and grounding agents support execution, with component ablations on Linux and Windows GUI tasks.

name: Agentic World Modeling: Foundations, Capabilities, Laws, and Beyond
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Web and GUI agents are one part of a survey that also covers physical, social, and scientific settings.
summary: Survey of agentic world models that classifies predictive capabilities and governing laws, including the digital setting of web and GUI agents.

name: OS-SPEAR: A Toolkit for the Safety, Performance,Efficiency, and Robustness Analysis of OS Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Provides an evaluation toolkit for joint safety, efficiency, and multimodal robustness analysis of operating-system GUI agents.

name: AutoGUI-v2: A Comprehensive Multi-Modal GUI Functionality Understanding Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AutoGUI-v2 evaluates interface functionality, grounding and predicted interaction outcomes using hierarchical regions derived through VLM-human annotation. Its tasks span multiple operating systems and expose differences between functional localization, captioning and transition-logic understanding.

name: Odysseys: Benchmarking Web Agents on Realistic Long Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces Odysseys, a live-web benchmark of long, multi-site tasks derived from browsing sessions. Graded task rubrics and a rubric-score-per-step measure evaluate both partial progress and trajectory efficiency.

name: Benchmarking and Improving GUI Agents in High-Dynamic Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces DynamicGUIBench for applications whose interfaces change between actions, together with DynamicUI, an agent that processes screen recordings. The agent selects informative frames, filters inconsistent action reasoning and uses trajectory reflection for subsequent decisions.

name: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SnapGuard detects screenshot-based prompt injection through complementary visual-stability and recovered textual cues. Its evaluation compares detection quality and inference cost across attack and benign-page settings.

name: Training Computer Use Agents to Assess the Usability of Graphical User Interfaces
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: uxCUA learns to assess interface usability by choosing interaction flows, executing them and predicting a numerical usability score. Training uses interactive UIs with usability labels and human preferences, with evaluations on synthetic and real interfaces.

name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.

name: AutoSurfer -- Teaching Web Agents through Comprehensive Surfing, Learning, and Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AutoSurfer explores website actions breadth-first, retaining page and trajectory knowledge to guide task synthesis and trajectory refinement. It evaluates the resulting training data by fine-tuning a web agent on WebArena and examining synthesized-task diversity.

name: WindowsWorld: A Process-Centric Benchmark of Autonomous GUI Agents in Professional Cross-Application Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Desktop use is explicit; no additional operating-system claim is inferred solely from the benchmark name.
summary: Introduces WindowsWorld for professional workflows spanning multiple desktop applications, with generated tasks refined through human review. Intermediate subgoals support process-oriented evaluation of cross-application reasoning and execution efficiency.

name: FineState-Bench: Benchmarking State-Conditioned Grounding for Fine-grained GUI State Setting
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark measures exact target-state setting; the abstract reports low exact goal-state success.
summary: FineState-Bench tests whether GUI agents locate the intended control and set its exact state across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces, with stage-wise diagnostic metrics.

name: Exploring LLM Agent Designs and Interaction Modalities for Scientific Visualization
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study compares specialized, computer-use and coding agents on scientific visualization workflows. It examines GUI, CLI, code and tool-call interaction modes, including how persistent memory changes performance across repeated trials.

name: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: A11y-Compressor transforms linearized accessibility trees through modal detection, redundancy reduction and semantic structuring. Its OSWorld evaluation measures both observation-token reduction and task success.

name: AcademiClaw: When Students Set Challenges for AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: AcademiClaw benchmarks OpenClaw agents on long academic workflows, scoring task completion in isolated Docker sandboxes with rubrics and a safety audit.

name: Augmenting Interface Usability Heuristics for Reliable Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The agent results come from controlled UI-Verse environments.
summary: A study adapts interface usability heuristics for computer-use agents and evaluates augmented designs in UI-Verse, a suite of controlled interface environments.

name: WAAA! Web Adversaries Against Agentic Browsers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates agentic browsers against classical web attacks and visual social-engineering lures beyond indirect prompt injection.

name: Computer Use at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). DigiWorld comprises 15 sandboxed mobile applications.
summary: DigiWorld is a sandboxed mobile-app benchmark for computer-use agents, paired with PRISM environment principles and a confidence-interval aggregation method.

name: OTora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework for Reasoning-Level Denial-of-Service in LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). WebShop is one of several agent settings used to evaluate the general attack framework.
summary: OTora generates attacks that increase reasoning and tool use in multi-step LLM agents while preserving task outcomes; evaluations include WebShop agents.

name: Don't Click That: Teaching Web Agents to Resist Deceptive Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DUDE combines asymmetric hybrid-reward learning with summaries of deceptive-interface failures to guide safer web actions. Its RUC benchmark evaluates deception susceptibility alongside ordinary task performance across interface scenarios.

name: How Mobile World Model Guides GUI Agents?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares mobile world models that predict state changes as delta text, full text, images or renderable code. Downstream Android benchmarks examine synthetic training trajectories and test-time guidance, including limits of post-action reflection.

name: WildClawBench: A Benchmark for Real-World, Long-Horizon Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: WildClawBench evaluates CLI agents on long, multimodal tasks in Docker containers with real tools, using task checks, side-effect audits, and a semantic judge.

name: MMTB: Evaluating Terminal Agents on Multimedia-File Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent computer-automation benchmark using terminal workflows, explicitly separated from graphical-interface control.
summary: MultiMedia-TerminalBench evaluates agents that use terminal tools to work with audio and video files. The Terminus-MM harness adds multimedia perception to study how accessible evidence changes executable workflows and task outcomes.

name: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: LongMemEval-V2 asks memory systems to recover environment knowledge from long web-agent histories for question answering. Its AgentRunbook variants contrast indexed knowledge pools with coding-agent retrieval from stored trajectory files.

name: Covering Human Action Space for Computer Use: Data Synthesis and Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CUActSpot to evaluate clicks, drags, drawing and other screen interactions across GUI, text, tables, canvases and natural images. A renderer-based pipeline records geometry and screenshots, then generates matching instructions and action traces for training a grounding model.

name: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Re-Prefill adds an attention-guided second prefill pass that revisits candidate screen regions before coordinate generation. The study evaluates this training-free intervention across GUI-grounding models and benchmarks.

name: Beyond Binary: Reframing GUI Critique as Continuous Semantic Alignment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: BBCritic ranks candidate GUI-agent actions through instruction–action alignment, while BBBench evaluates fine-grained ranking with a hierarchical action taxonomy.

name: Orchard: An Open-Source Agentic Modeling Framework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The computer-use agent is one of three recipes in a broader agentic modeling framework.
summary: Orchard provides an environment service and training recipes for several agent domains, including Orchard-GUI, a vision-language computer-use agent.

name: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
notes: The complete retained official abstract and cached official README were reviewed.
summary: SaaS-Bench evaluates browser agents on professional workflows across self-hosted applications. Weighted checkpoints measure task completion and partial progress, with application-state checks and configured content judges documented in the official harness.

name: PAGER: Bridging the Semantic-Execution Gap in Point-Precise Geometric GUI Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PAGE Bench for point-precise geometric GUI construction and PAGER, an agent that plans around primitive dependencies and executes pixel-level actions.

name: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its agent evaluation uses generated tasks in sandbox shops.
summary: ShopGym builds sandbox e-commerce storefronts from live shops and generates catalog-grounded tasks for evaluating web shopping agents in resettable environments.

name: WinDeskGround: A Benchmark for Robust GUI Grounding in Complex Multi-Window Desktop Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WinDeskGround synthesizes multi-window desktop layouts with controlled occlusion, density and semantic similarity to test GUI grounding robustness. Its instruction-target benchmark measures how localization changes when interfaces depart from simple single-layer scenes.

name: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SE-GA retrieves hierarchical memories during inference and uses the collected experience in a separate policy-improvement pipeline. Its evaluation includes offline grounding/action tasks and online Android interaction, which measure different capabilities.

name: DiagEval: Trajectory-Conditioned Diagnosis for Reliable Software Evaluation with GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: DiagEval diagnoses failed GUI-agent evaluations of interactive software by reusing failed trajectories for targeted probes that distinguish execution errors from defects.

name: MUIAnno: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark for Mobile UI Understanding
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MUIAnno provides expert labels for elements in manually explored mobile-app screens, with a web annotation tool that emits structured JSON. It also supplies UI-element detection baselines for the dataset.

name: DocOS: Towards Proactive Document-Guided Actions in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DocOS benchmarks agents that search online documentation and translate procedural instructions into GUI actions in interactive web environments. It separates failures to retrieve useful procedures from failures to ground retrieved instructions into executable actions.

name: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. It also converts computer-use traces into controller training data and evaluates semantic actions, progress and memory consistency on long-horizon tasks.

name: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OmniGUI evaluates step-level action prediction from interleaved smartphone screenshots, synchronous audio and video. Expert demonstrations carry multimodal-dependency annotations, and initial baselines use native multimodal models as agent proxies to study temporal and audio-related failures.

name: CutVerse: A Compositional GUI Agents Benchmark for Media Post-Production Editing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Cutverse benchmarks GUI agents on long editing workflows across professional media applications and parses recordings and input logs into grounded action trajectories.

name: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OpenComputer, which builds desktop tasks around application-state verifiers and refines those verifiers using execution feedback. An evaluation harness records trajectories and assigns auditable partial credit across professional software workflows.

name: MemGym: a Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Computer use is one track among dialogue, research, and coding evaluations.
summary: MemGym benchmarks agent memory across several task regimes, including computer use on WebArena-Infinity, with scores designed to isolate memory performance.

name: Spreadsheet-RL: Advancing Large Language Model Agents on Realistic Spreadsheet Tasks via Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Spreadsheet-RL trains spreadsheet agents with RL in a Microsoft Excel environment exposed through a Python sandbox and supplies the Domain-Spreadsheet benchmark.

name: ScaleWoB: Guiding GUI Agents with Coding Agents via Large-Scale Environmental Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Mobile, desktop and automotive interfaces are simulated as webpages.
summary: Introduces ScaleWoB, which synthesizes interactive GUI environments as backend-free webpages with verifiable rewards. Its mobile-oriented benchmark evaluates agent execution and compares selected synthetic tasks with real-app behavior.

name: AgentHijack: Benchmarking Computer Use Agent Robustness to Common Environment Corruptions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AgentHijack, a benchmark for desktop computer-use agents facing pop-ups, resolution changes and other common corruptions, alongside an agent that checks its environment.

name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.

name: MobileGym: A Verifiable and Highly Parallel Simulation Platform for Mobile GUI Agent Research
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The simulator is browser-hosted.
summary: Introduces MobileGym, a browser-hosted simulation of mobile app interactions whose configurable JSON state supports deterministic judging and parallel rollouts. MobileGym-Bench adds parameterized tasks, with experiments examining online training and transfer to real devices.

name: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent GUI-application generation benchmark with real component interaction probes; its main evaluated agents are application coders.
summary: VISTA evaluates coding agents that turn design handoffs into working web and Android applications. Its evaluator locates annotated interactive components and probes their behavior, keeping visual localization distinct from functional correctness.

name: Anchor: Preventing Artifact Drift for Reliable Agent Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The shared verifier scores end-state business correctness across several agent harnesses.
summary: Anchor builds ERP-Bench by generating procurement and manufacturing tasks with shared state verifiers for evaluating browser and computer-use agents.

name: ChartAct: A Benchmark for Dynamic Chart Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: ChartAct benchmarks multimodal models and GUI agents on interactive charts from websites, requiring actions such as hovering or zooming to answer questions.

name: Scaling, Benchmarking, and Reasoning of Vision-Language Agents for Mobile GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUIEvalKit benchmarks offline navigation tasks.
summary: HyperTrack provides mobile GUI navigation tasks across Chinese apps, while GUIEvalKit benchmarks VLM agents offline and supports analysis of training scale and history.

name: AndroidDaily: A Verifiable Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents on Real-World Closed-Source Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AndroidDaily evaluates mobile GUI agents on daily workflows in closed-source Android apps. Its GRADE evaluator follows visual trajectories against operational obligations, output-quality requirements and negative constraints, producing process-level diagnostics without hidden app state.

name: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MIRAGE constructs mobile screenshot injections in ordinary user-content regions through localization, contextual payload generation and realism curation. Its evaluation separates visual realism from attack effectiveness against pixel-observing GUI agents.

name: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. GUI agents actually load and play browser-game builds, providing an executable interface-testing signal for game-code generation; the central application remains game development.
summary: PlaytestArena evaluates generated browser games using expected in-play behaviors adjudicated by GUI agents. Play2Code pairs a coding agent with a rubric-blind GUI playtester whose interaction traces and feedback guide iterative refinement, with a separate final judge.

name: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MaskClaw makes local Allow, Mask or Ask decisions before GUI screenshots leave a trusted environment, using visual evidence and personalized policy memory. Its benchmark and designed evolution scenarios test how corrections and edits can become privacy skills checked by a sandbox gate.

name: GTA: Generating Long-Horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GTA generates multi-hop web-agent tasks and executable trajectories through crawling, retrieval, and validation, releasing a benchmark built from over 50 websites.

name: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents: Comprehensive Evaluation with a Lightweight Framework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a lightweight framework for evaluating HTML reduction in web agents, using Minimal Failure Set coverage to assess pruning and optimize latency.

name: Recovering Policy-Induced Errors: Benchmarking and Trajectory Synthesis for Robust GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GUI-RobustEval measures how GUI agents recover from their own errors, while RoTS synthesizes recovery trajectories for training on varied failure modes.

name: PhoneWorld: From Real-App Trajectories to Dynamic and Verifiable Environments for Phone-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces PhoneWorld, which converts observed app pages, transitions and state changes into executable Android environments through a build-inspect-repair process. Generated tasks and programmatic verifiers support benchmarking, trajectory collection and online training.

name: DiffSpot: Can VLMs Spot Fine-Grained Visual Differences in Web Interfaces?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: DiffSpot benchmarks detection of fine visual changes in rendered web interfaces using image pairs created by single-property CSS mutations.

name: BlueFin: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces BlueFin, a benchmark and evaluation framework for agents handling professional finance spreadsheet workbooks through synthesis, manipulation, and comprehension tasks.

name: Masking Stale Observations Helps Search Agents -- Until It Doesn't: A Regime Map and Its Mechanism
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies when masking older retrieved pages helps long-horizon search agents manage context, using offline and live-web search benchmarks and analysis of reopened pages.

name: OpenWebRL: Demystifying Online Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning for Visual Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports results on Online-Mind2Web and DeepShop.
summary: Introduces OpenWebRL, a framework for training visual web agents with online multi-turn reinforcement learning on live websites, including browser infrastructure and success judging.

name: Context-Aware Workflow Decomposition for Automated Mobile UI Annotation Using Multimodal Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The experiments use expert-annotated screens from MUIAnno.
summary: Studies staged prompting for automated mobile UI element annotation, comparing workflow depths and element groupings on expert-annotated MUIAnno screens.

name: DeskCraft: Benchmarking Desktop Agents on Professional Workflows and Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DeskCraft evaluates professional desktop workflows and human-agent collaboration through mid-execution clarification, interruption and post-completion feedback. Its tasks cover creative applications and expose difficulties in long-horizon execution and proactive clarification.

name: MedCUA-Bench: A Screenshot-Only Benchmark for Clinical Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MedCUA-Bench evaluates screenshot-only clinical interface workflows using paired intent- and step-level goals. It combines reconstructed medical interfaces with completion and clinical-safety checks, and separately reports results on a real OpenEMR system.

name: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LivingScreen evaluates agents in a browser-based short-video environment where observing content consumes time and affects subsequent actions. Its task suite scores accuracy together with information efficiency to diagnose over- and under-observation on continuously changing screens.

name: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CUA-HandCrafted, a browser-agent red-teaming benchmark that varies attack templates, tasks and system prompts. Its domain comparison and reproducibility audit caution against transferring browser-surface safety conclusions to coding agents or unreleased optimized injections.

name: PerceptUI: LLM Agents as Human-Aligned Synthetic Users for UI/UX Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PerceptUI, a persona-conditioned model for predicting how particular users answer questions about interfaces, supporting synthetic UI/UX evaluation.

name: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DragOn supplies drag-grounding training data and a held-out benchmark for highlighting text, selecting cells, resizing elements and moving sliders. It evaluates existing vision-language models and a model fine-tuned on the drag tasks.

name: MacArena: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on an Online macOS Environment
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MacArena runs computer-use tasks through Apple’s virtualization framework on Apple Silicon, combining task ports with macOS-native workloads. It distinguishes the ported and native subsets when examining agent performance and cross-platform transfer.
