name: StainFlow: Entity-Stain Tracking and Evidence Linking for Process Rewards in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: StainFlow tracks visually verifiable task entities through GUI trajectories to identify phases and retrieve focused evidence windows. Its process-reward model is tested for both online policy learning and trajectory-completion judgments.

name: WeaveBench: A Long-Horizon, Real-World Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents with Hybrid Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WeaveBench requires agents to combine GUI, command-line and code operations within long tasks on an Ubuntu desktop. A trajectory-aware judge checks deliverables and interaction evidence, including shortcut behavior that outcome-only grading can miss.

name: AliyunConsoleAgent: Training Web Agents in Real-World Cloud Environments via Distillation and Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: AliyunConsoleAgent trains browser agents to verify documented procedures against changing cloud-console UIs through trajectory distillation and online GRPO. Provisioned rollout environments and backend audit-log checks support training and outcome evaluation.

name: iOSWorld: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Phone Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a native iOS simulator benchmark with persistent user data, multi-app tasks, and personalization-dependent phone workflows.

name: Workflow-GYM: Towards Long-Horizon Evaluation of Computer-use Agentic tasks in Real-World Professional Fields
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Workflow-GYM evaluates long GUI workflows in professional software. Its analysis examines failures such as omitted stages, accumulated errors and goal drift during specialized end-to-end work.

name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.

name: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UXBench for diagnosing usability issues from UI screenshots and UI-UX, a reinforcement-trained model for reasoning about those interface problems.

name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.

name: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: StakeBench evaluates prompt-injection harm to different stakeholders in shopping web-agent workflows. Its executable cases separate attack objectives and assess both outcomes and execution processes to reveal how the same attack pattern can affect different parties.

name: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluation injects seven deceptive patterns into existing web environments.
summary: Introduces WebDecept, a plugin for injecting deceptive e-commerce interface patterns during web-agent tasks and evaluating how multimodal agents respond.

name: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a benchmark and online evaluation method for predicting the next spreadsheet action from a user's action history, using curated action sequences.

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.

name: Running the Gauntlet: Hard Agentic Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). The benchmark uses five controlled web-based professional applications.
summary: Introduces GauntletBench, a web-based benchmark of vision-intensive tasks in five professional applications for assessing agent perception, 3D reasoning, and generalisation.

name: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PhoneHarness routes phone workflows across GUI actions, device-side commands and host tools while retaining auditable execution traces. Its accompanying benchmark checks observable task side effects, separating mixed-action execution from plausible final-answer generation.

name: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares online skill and memory augmentations with a vanilla web agent given the same total inference-token budget. Across WebArena and WorkArena settings, it studies when module overhead removes aggregate gains and how rerun variability changes conclusions.

name: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates action-level guardrails and full computer tasks with environment-dependent safety constraints, separating safe completion from nominal success.

name: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its state tracking relies on websites exposing a deterministic semantic MDP.
summary: Introduces WebStep, a web-agent benchmark that records semantic states behind GUI interactions to analyze exploration, execution accuracy, and decisive errors across task steps.

name: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: FraudSMSWalker tests browser agents on bilingual SMS-to-webpage fraud judgments while hiding URL and reputation shortcuts. Its controlled chains include difficult benign login/payment cases and evaluate whether classifications remain supported by the visible message and page evidence.

name: MyPCBench: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MyPCBench tests personal-assistant tasks on a Linux desktop with simulated web applications and data for a single fictional persona. A shared computer-and-shell interface enables evaluation of cross-application workflows that depend on personal context and account-like state.

name: LabOSBench: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents for Scientific Instrument Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LabOSBench evaluates GUI agents on browser-based scientific instrument simulators with configurable tasks and execution-based checks. Its subtask and end-to-end tests examine feedback-driven adjustment and long workflows without controlling physical instruments.

name: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ProCUA-SFT generates tasks and synthetic trajectories on live desktops seeded with document content, checking task preconditions before rollout. The resulting step-prefix examples are formatted to match inference context and used for supervised GUI-agent fine-tuning.

name: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for GUI coordinate generation under student-produced prefixes. A correctness-aware gate suppresses coordinate-token supervision outside the target box, while teacher-probability scaling adjusts the remaining signal strength.

name: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: HANSEL extracts evidence pages and snippets from browser-agent traces and preserves relevant page state in interactive verification views. It flags untraceable answers and evaluates evidence selection and human verification effort separately.

name: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: This study compares general coding agents using mobile command-line access with reproducible GUI agents on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld. It also supplies oracle CLI analyses and a separate task suite for operations such as bulk changes, filtering and hidden device state.

name: MobileForge: Annotation-Free Adaptation for Mobile GUI Agents with Hierarchical Feedback-Guided Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MobileForge couples real-app exploration and generated tasks with hierarchical feedback for mobile-agent adaptation. Its optimizer turns trajectory outcomes, step feedback and corrective hints into contextualized GRPO updates, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and a GUI-only MobileWorld split.

name: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Segments and clusters GUI trajectories into inspectable skills, then trains a skill-aware policy from those annotations. Its diagnostic results distinguish readable source-domain clusters from reliable transfer and report limited or absent downstream gains.

name: OctoNest: Adaptive Cross-Device Execution through Stateful Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces OctoNest, which coordinates device agents, revises task assignments from execution feedback, and switches local interaction modalities; CAPEBench evaluates cross-device tasks.

name: Darwin Mobile Agent: A Roadmap for Self-Evolution
notes: The implemented stage uses selected tasks, an external judge and heuristic history management. Autonomous curricula, verification and memory are roadmap directions. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (2 Agent-Environment Interface and Policy Optimisation; 3 Scalable Asynchronous Mobile Environment; 3.2 Persistent State Management; 3.3 Task Lifecycle; 4.2 Rollout and Optimisation; 4.3 Anatomy of the Self-Evolving Agent).
summary: Describes asynchronous reinforcement-learning infrastructure using parallel cloud-hosted Android instances, explicit task lifecycles, and persistent-state management for mobile GUI interaction.

name: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MIRAGE evaluates targeted next-action hijacking from adversarial images restricted to legitimate third-party webpage regions. It combines diffusion-based image generation with execution-aware optimization and tests the constrained visual-injection setting on web-agent frameworks.

name: When Web Agents Finish but Still Fail: Reproducible Triggers and Trace Diagnostics for Parallel Web Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark concerns parallel web exploration and answer synthesis.
summary: Introduces Parallel WebBench for parallel web exploration and uses verified URL trajectories to diagnose search loops, incomplete answers, and failures after evidence retrieval.

name: Fara-1.5: Scalable Learning Environments for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Builds browser-agent training trajectories with live and synthetic environments, solvers, user simulation, and complementary correctness and efficiency verifiers.

name: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Builds a logging framework that combines network/protocol fingerprints with browser interaction behavior to attribute web-agent traffic. A decision-tree classifier is evaluated across six agent implementations, human browsing and conventional crawlers.

name: ChainWorld: Composing Long-Horizon Desktop Workloads from Atomic OSWorld Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ChainWorld composes compatible atomic OSWorld tasks into multi-objective desktop chains while preserving their evaluators. It compares giving the full sequence at once with revealing goals turn by turn, exposing different state and session-management failures.

name: MacAgentBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Real-World macOS Desktop
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces macOS tasks spanning GUI and command-line interaction, with deterministic checks and intermediate-progress scoring for application workflows.

name: Agent MechSuits: Mechanistic Subspace Safety Steering for Multi-Turn CLI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces Agent MechSuits, a framework that detects unsafe states and steers multi-turn CLI agents through hidden-representation interventions, alongside the MAS trajectory benchmark.

name: When AUC 0.998 Is Not Enough: A Candidate Evaluation Protocol for Hidden-State Probes of Indirect Prompt Injection in Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Proposes diagnostic controls for hidden-state probes of indirect prompt injection in multimodal computer-use agents, using a teacher-forced Mind2Web case study.

name: ENVS: Environment-Native Verified Search for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: ENVS branches over GUI actions in live desktop VMs, verifies successful leaves, and converts them into balanced step-level training supervision. It also introduces OSWorld-Noisy to test recovery from dynamic interruptions while retaining the underlying tasks.

name: Capable but Careless: Do Computer-Use Agents Follow Contextual Integrity?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AgentCIBench evaluates whether computer-use agents disclose information in ways that violate its original context. Deterministically scored scenarios test nearby sensitive UI content, ambiguous requests and recipient mismatches, including end-to-end agent execution.

name: Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: The framework uses a vision-language judge’s final-screen assessment as a terminal reward for GUI reinforcement learning. It models evaluator noise and corrects the reward estimator used by PPO across desktop benchmarks.

name: VisCritic: Visual State Comparison as Process Reward for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VisCritic compares before/after screenshots through change-aware visual features and an action-conditioned critic. Weakly supervised samples from existing traces train judgments of action success, progress and error type for GUI-agent verification.

name: GUI vs. CLI: Execution Bottlenecks in Screen-Only and Skill-Mediated Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This benchmark matches desktop goals, initial states and final-state verifiers across screen-only GUI and skill-mediated CLI agents. Its experiments separate graphical execution failures from missing CLI skill coverage, including a verifier-guided skill-augmentation condition.

name: Uncertainty Quantification for Computer-Use Agents: A Benchmark across Vision-Language Models and GUI Grounding Datasets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Argus benchmarks post-hoc uncertainty methods for single-step GUI grounding across open-weight and closed-source observation regimes. It tests calibration, rejection, error severity and conformal click regions, finding that uncertainty rankings transfer less reliably across model/interface regimes than across datasets for one model.

name: Ko-WideSearch: A Korean Breadth-Search Benchmark for Exhaustive Set Enumeration by Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its tasks assess exhaustive web search and table answers.
summary: Introduces Ko-WideSearch, a Korean web-agent benchmark that asks agents to find every member of a set and fill a table of attributes for each member.

name: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent general computer-operation benchmark evaluated through a terminal.
summary: TUA-Bench evaluates terminal-use agents on general digital tasks, including document editing, email, web information seeking and specialist software workflows. Tasks run in real terminals with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.

name: Bridging VideoQA and Video-Guided Agentic Tasks via Generalized Keyframe Extraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces VG-GUIBench to evaluate GUI agents following video tutorials, and TASKER to select task-relevant keyframes for video-guided tasks and VideoQA.

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

name: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces extended computer-use workflows with realistic artifacts, changing information, hidden state, and partial-progress and safety assessments.

name: SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SpreadsheetBench 2, a benchmark of multi-sheet business spreadsheet workflows for agents, covering generation, debugging, and visualization tasks.

name: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.

name: On the Internet, Nobody Knows You're an LLM Bot: Unmasking Web Agents with Multi-Layer Fingerprinting
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Evaluates web agents against anti-bot mechanisms on instrumented honeysites and analyzes network, HTTP and browser fingerprints. The study compares resistance to blocking with the ability to distinguish agents, humans and agent implementations.

name: PPT-Eval: A Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents on PowerPoint Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PPT-Eval, a benchmark of PowerPoint creation and editing tasks for computer-use agents, with rubrics that score partial progress and presentation quality.

name: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Uses failed computer-use trajectories to diagnose failure modes and generate inference-time agent code patches, with light human verification. An OSWorld study evaluates this failure-driven improvement loop without additional model training.

name: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.

name: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? Diagnosing State-Belief Reliance on Pixels versus Structure
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Defines visual state reliance and probes whether GUI agents resolve screenshot/structure conflicts using pixels, serialized interface structure or prior beliefs. Paired interventions and live multi-step tests connect misattributed state beliefs to failures and compare consistency-based mitigations.

name: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study examines agent data injection, where untrusted content impersonates trusted metadata or tool-context data. It reports arbitrary-click vulnerabilities in web agents alongside separate coding-agent attacks, highlighting trust-boundary failures beyond instruction injection.

name: WebRetriever: A Large-Scale Comprehensive Benchmark for Efficient Web Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebRetriever evaluates navigation, knowledge-assisted interaction and end-to-end information-extraction workflows under separate protocols. Its NavEval judge uses richer interaction context to diagnose cases where navigation success and useful task completion diverge.

name: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UniClawBench, a benchmark of proactive agents on bilingual real-world tasks, evaluated in live Docker containers with stepwise checkpoints and simulated user feedback.

name: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MAG jointly evaluates browser task actions and user-facing guides grounded in screenshots through element marks or pixel coordinates. Its harness covers annotation, live evaluation and joint metrics, with an expert-trajectory-augmented GRPO training study.

name: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.

name: Designing Agent-Ready Websites for AI Web Agents: A Framework for Machine Readability, Actionability, and Decision Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison uses two versions of one website prototype in a controlled experiment.
summary: Proposes an agent-ready website design framework for e-commerce browser agents and compares it with a human-oriented site on shopping tasks, outcomes, steps, and token use.

name: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies a controlled setting where GRPO fails to improve a strong small web agent and can reduce text-track performance. Matched reachable-reward tasks and component grafting distinguish limited optimization headroom from learning-rate-dependent failure mechanisms.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.

name: Just A Rather Very Intelligent Spoken Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces JarvisBench, a benchmark for spoken mediation during long-horizon agent workflows, measuring task collaboration and how users follow ongoing execution.

name: EvoGUI: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for GUI State-Transition Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces EvoGUI, which derives temporal ordering, inverse action/value prediction, and successor-discrimination probes from recorded GUI trajectories. Its web-derived benchmark isolates transition understanding from the other abilities involved in end-to-end task success.

name: Teach it to stop, not just to click
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The repair study uses five oracle-graded environments; task-level transfer is reported for a case where one corrective action remains.
summary: Studies verifier-guided repair of a 35B computer-use agent across five environments, examining variation across runs and data draws in done detection, GUI clicks, and field entry.

name: Broken Gates: Re-evaluating Web Bot Defenses in the Age of LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Measures how autonomous LLM browser agents interact with commercial bot-management and anti-automation defenses on the web.

name: DocOps: A Verifiable Benchmark for Autonomous Agents in Complex Document Operations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces DocOps, a verifiable benchmark for agents handling complex digital-document workflows, with analysis of state tracking, semantic checks, and structural edits.

name: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents using browsing histories, and PACMem, a structured memory method for guiding navigation.

name: Beyond Sequential Interaction: Benchmarking Parallel Execution and Coordination for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces ParaGUIBench, with tasks and efficiency measurements for coordinated GUI agents operating separate desktop instances over a shared file system. Its ParaGUI planner-worker system decomposes tasks and dispatches concurrent subtasks for comparison with serial execution.

name: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SeekJudge, which iteratively searches and analyzes GUI trajectories to assess instruction fulfillment. The work combines dense judgment-data synthesis, a step-label benchmark, and reward-server scheduling to study accurate and practical reward feedback for agent training.

name: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces an Interactive Reward Agent that proposes completion conditions and verifies them using system, application, and GUI tools after execution. GUI-RewardBench provides annotated desktop trajectories for evaluating these evidence-based judgments and their use in reinforcement learning.

name: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Desktop-Delta Bench, an offline diagnostic of GUI transition understanding using temporal-ordering tasks and before/after action inference. It includes decoy observations to test whether models track the source and task relevance of screen changes.

name: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark for long-horizon office-suite agent tasks with labor-time and price signals, plus rubric-based code verifiers.

name: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Audits failure-scored computer-use trajectories to distinguish agent errors from broken tasks and evaluator false negatives. It organizes reliability issues across task construction, trajectory evidence, scoring, and reporting, then derives corresponding evaluation design practices.

name: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Examines inference-time scaling for local computer-use models by varying context, step budgets, decomposition, and parallel execution. OSWorld experiments track both task performance and changing failure modes, exposing cases where extra computation extends errors or adds coordination overhead.

name: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces OSReward and its harder and multidimensional variants for assessing judgments of computer-use trajectories. It also releases a reasoning-annotated judgment corpus and trains reward models, examining reliability, leniency bias, and evaluation cost.

name: Alignment Is Local: A Paired Diagnostic for GUI Agents under User-Side Persuasion
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Presents a paired diagnostic of prompt guardrails in GUI agents under screen-grounded user persuasion, comparing single-turn probes with four-turn escalation.

name: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). OSWorld~2.0 is one evaluation setting alongside WeaveBench and Terminal-Bench~2.1.
summary: Introduces LongHorizon-Harness, which maintains verified task state outside an agent's execution context and audits subtasks; its evaluations include OSWorld~2.0.

name: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). HITLCUA simulates human participation through an API-simulated user.
summary: Introduces II-Bench for low-harm indirect prompt injections against computer-use agents and HITLCUA for testing them in virtual-machine and web environments with simulated user review.

name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.

name: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: CUADebug combines a failure taxonomy and human-annotated OSWorld failure trajectories with an agent that locates causal steps and proposes corrections from screenshots and action traces. It evaluates root-cause diagnosis separately from controlled task re-execution and failure recovery.

name: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUI-Lens uses OCR and detected interface components as coordinate references while a general-purpose VLM selects progressively enlarged screenshot crops. Instruction-conditioned checks constrain the crop and click proposals before mapping the final location back to the original screen.

name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study separates tool-adoption behavior from task competence in hybrid GUI–MCP agents. It tests tool-use incentives and screenshot-history compression, showing that changed action preferences can coexist with unchanged held-out accuracy.

name: MissClick: Execution-Aware Adversarial Attacks on Coordinate Generation in GUI Grounding Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MissClick designs white-box attacks around the numerical effect of coordinate digits on executable GUI clicks. Separate untargeted displacement and targeted place-weighted objectives are evaluated across desktop, web and mobile grounding settings.

name: LoginTrap: Uncovering Task-Agnostic Phishing-Style Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks against LLM-based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces LoginTrap, a black-box indirect-injection evaluation in which attacker-controlled page context and login flows induce unauthorized authentication. It measures end-to-end private-data leakage across web-agent backbones, architectures and defenses.

name: "Allow" to Achieve, Over-Privileged Inadvertently: The Unintended Cost of Task-Completion-Driven Pop-up Decisions in Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This permission-literacy study tests whether mobile GUI agents grant only task-necessary permissions. Controlled changes to task context and requester identity expose authorization biases and the trade-off between suppressing unnecessary and legitimate grants.

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.

name: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Measures the complementarity, cost and rerun variability of six browser observation modes on WebArena and VisualWebArena. Its routing experiments distinguish an oracle cost opportunity from policies that fail to robustly outperform a fixed observation mode.

name: WebGrader: Training LLMs for Web Development with Self-Evolving Programmatic Grader
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces WebGrader, a programmatic grader for website generation that plans interaction flows, runs them in a live browser, and uses observed outcomes as RL rewards.

name: StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported attack results depend on agents following a chain of referenced pages.
summary: Introduces StepJack, a benchmark of indirect prompt injections that split an adversarial goal across pages on a computer-use agent's web navigation path.

name: WebRider: Persona-Conditioned Intent Controllers for Live-Web Assistance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). RiderBench evaluates live-web contracts across 42 public websites.
summary: Introduces WebRider, a live-web agent that maintains intent contracts while carrying out guarded browser actions, and RiderBench for auditing those contracts across websites.

name: SynChain: Inducing Computer-Use Agent Systems to Construct Their Own Attack Chains
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SynChain, an attack that induces persistent agents to create poisoned skills or memory entries, and CUAChain for evaluating later attack-chain activation.

name: AndroidReality: How Far Are Mobile Agents from the Real World?
notes: The reviewed protocol normally activates one perturbation type at a time while preserving task semantics and reward. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.1 Perturbation formulation; 3.2 Injection; 3.3 Evaluation protocol; 4.3 Error analysis).
summary: Extends AndroidWorld with controlled state, transition, and action perturbations to test mobile-agent robustness, and studies a training-free introspective recovery mechanism.

name: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark covers formulas, charts, pivot tables, and conditional formatting in spreadsheets.
summary: Introduces the workbook time machine to create spreadsheet-object tasks and wtmbench to evaluate spreadsheet manipulation agents using different control interfaces.

name: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: CAP builds cross-site browser workflows by decomposing websites into operation and perception requirements and recomposing them into tasks. Its judge-based evaluation diagnoses complex interactions and visual-perception failures across real websites.

name: Software Engineering for and with GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Surveys 336 GUI-agent papers through a software engineering lens, covering architectures, evaluation, and lifecycle concerns in mobile and web settings.

name: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This framework separates frozen-model instruction expansion from a trained layout-aware matcher that localizes GUI elements without coordinate regression. Binary text/icon supervision supports the matcher, with evaluations on GUI grounding and Mind2Web element-selection tasks.

name: Navigation Alone Is Not Enough: Evaluating Explanatory Assistive UI Agents
notes: Packaged tasks use recorded linear transition graphs. Reported model experiments use a text-input validation subset; their results measure that subset. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.3 Interface states and task annotations; 3.4 Evaluation; 4.1 Models and experimental setup; 5 Discussion).
summary: Introduces NeXUI, an assistive UI-agent benchmark that evaluates navigation together with interface-grounded explanations and user oversight in recorded interface states.

name: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
notes: The paper abstract and official project README were reviewed. The README documents an Ubuntu desktop and GUI action interface and includes LLM-assisted evaluators.
summary: DSAgentBench evaluates end-to-end data-science workflows spanning analysis, modeling and visualization inside a real desktop environment. Task evaluators check produced analytical and visual artifacts, while the released interface supports screenshot or accessibility observations and GUI actions.

name: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MobileJudgeBench compares completion judges against human labels on mobile-agent trajectories. It studies screenshot-sampling baselines, model-dependent error profiles and how judge quality relates to agent rankings and reinforcement-learning rewards.

name: LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LegacyWorld evaluates Windows GUI workflows under an atomicity criterion: finish correctly or fail without persistent unintended changes. It compares expert prompts with prompts derived from recorded golden paths and separates useful completion, safe failure and non-atomic side effects.

name: Act2Intention: A Benchmark For Developing Active Mobile Agents Through Inferring User Intention from GUI Actions
notes: The benchmark combines real and generated trajectory material. Opportune intervention timing and real-user acceptance are stated limitations. Section 4.2.2 specifies Android emulator instances for generated action trajectories. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3 Task definition; 4.1 Raw data collection; 4.2 Trajectory construction; 7 Limitations and future directions).
summary: Introduces intention understanding, prediction, and confirmed execution tasks over mobile GUI trajectories, with a proactive agent combining personalized intention models and experience-guided actions.

name: Agentic ESOpt: Fine-Tuning Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Minimal GPU Requirements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebArena-Lite is one evaluation setting alongside automatic heuristic design.
summary: Introduces Agentic ESOpt, an evolution-strategies fine-tuning framework for long-horizon agents, evaluated on WebArena-Lite web tasks and automatic heuristic design.

name: MobileWorldSafety: Benchmarking GUI Agent Safety Against Environmental Injection Attacks in Android Apps
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates environmental injection risks in Android tasks using programmatic risk checks and model-based adjudication of ambiguous cases.

name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.

name: Automated Trajectory Evaluation for Mobile Agents via Step-Level Consequence Reasoning and Aggregation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluations use AndroidWorld for task completion and MobileRisk for safety.
summary: Introduces CRATE, a step-level visual judge for mobile-agent trajectories, and CRATE-S for assessing operational safety from action-conditioned state changes.

name: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies whether text-embedding GUI grounding scores reflect semantic matching or recovery of visible labels. Same-screen ranking comparisons with lexical baselines expose differences between deployable fusion, oracle selection, and performance on label-poor targets.

name: GUI-Primitives: Diagnosing Spatial Reasoning Failures in Vision-Language GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Primitives, a paired-instruction benchmark that changes a spatial relation while holding the screenshot and anchor fixed. Its diagnostics separate failure to localize either candidate from failure to choose the candidate satisfying the relation.

name: ClawProBench: Trace-Aware Evaluation of AI Agents with Runtime Coverage and Frozen Workplace-Style Holdouts
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces ClawProBench, a trace-aware benchmark for agents on OpenClaw that scores workspace and native-runtime tasks using execution traces, safety checks, and process quality.

name: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AnTrap, which injects task-solvable runtime anomalies into Android GUI-agent trajectories using a layered failure taxonomy. It compares model robustness and adversarial reinforcement learning to distinguish recoverable interface traps from persistent contextual failures.

name: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AdaptRubric, which retrieves reusable criteria for a GUI task family and then generates instruction-specific checks for concrete values and constraints. It evaluates these adaptive rubrics in offline reward assessment and online agent optimization.

name: ADeptS-Bench: Measuring the Trustworthiness of Computer Use Agents Across Devices
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates interface-embedded threats and whether computer-use agents seek clarification when mobile or desktop instructions are ambiguous.

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.

name: Benchmarking General Mobile Assistants in Challenging Real-World Scenarios
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its seven applications are based on open-source projects.
summary: Introduces GMA, a benchmark of 300 mobile-assistant tasks across seven applications, and studies how agent context retention and state tracking affect complex workflows.

name: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CURA, a telemetry-based runtime monitor that turns computer-use trajectories into sequential failure alarms and can trigger mid-task oversight. Its certificate controls false alarms, while the study separately reports detection performance and limits of retrospective monitoring.

name: ActReal: System-Level Mobile Agents Challenge Mobile Automation Detection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces ActReal, which translates semantic mobile-agent actions into coordinated touch and sensor signals to study automation-detection weaknesses. It evaluates detectors that observe touch events alone or together with inertial measurements under a privileged executor threat model.

name: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SIR, which iteratively refines a reusable library of prompt-injection strategies from failed computer-use attack trajectories. Its evaluation uses deterministic system-state checks and counts attacks only when the adversarial objective and legitimate task both complete.

name: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
notes: Adjacent browser-backed artifact validation evaluates generated artifacts and original-source recovery separately. Distinct from WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training.
summary: Uses typed browser interaction contracts to accept web-code improvements only when target progress and previously verified capabilities are preserved. Accepted transitions supply self-improvement data.

name: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-CC, a benchmark for assessing GUI world models as multi-step agent environments. Separate reference-action and agent-loop tracks test whether generated screens preserve context, plausible transitions, and task progress throughout interaction.

name: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: A diary study deploys the screen-reader-accessible OLLA computer-use prototype with blind users across desktop applications. Recorded commands and interaction traces support model comparisons and analysis of grounding, planning, constraint tracking and termination failures.

name: Monitoring Web Agents Without Internal Signals: Observable Trajectories and Key-Step Supervision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Predicts web-agent failure risk from observable trajectory prefixes using cross-step behavior and black-box consistency queries. Key-step labels preserve valid early prefixes of failed runs, and evaluation tests early intervention and transfer across website categories.

name: WiP: Characterizing and Defending Against Mobile-Agent-Driven MFA Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies how mobile automation can combine authentication factors within one agent environment and evaluates motion sensing as a user-presence signal.

name: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). GUI grounding is one evaluated task alongside optical character recognition.
summary: Introduces CA-OPD, a confidence-guided distillation method for visual prediction, evaluated on GUI grounding and optical character recognition benchmarks.

name: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains discriminative web world models to distinguish the true next state from outcomes of alternative actions. Branching web trajectories support training, followed by tests of predicted-state matching, process-reward action ranking and end-to-end WebArena-Lite selection.

name: Do GUI Agents Know When Not to Act? Enabling Conflict-Aware Termination for Multimodal GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: CONFLICTGUI evaluates termination under instruction conflicts and mismatches between instructions and interface context. CONFLICTGUARD couples feasibility checks with conditional action modulation to reduce unnecessary execution while tracking normal-task behavior.

name: ElderBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents for Older Adults
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ElderBench evaluates mobile GUI agents on smartphone requests elicited from older adults, including indirect and underspecified language. Online and offline tests, instruction normalization and linguistic analyses examine how these request patterns contribute to failures.

name: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. Controlled OSWorld comparisons examine both the benefits of shared procedural memory and its domain-dependent instability under repeated revision.

name: Beyond the Verdict: Evidence-Aligned Evaluation of Visual Prompt-Injection Guardrails
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Mind2Web-Injection, a benchmark for evaluating web-agent guardrail decisions on instruction-screenshot pairs using evidence boxes and image-side counterfactuals.

name: OmniStepBench: Deployment-Aware Agent Evaluation across Modalities and Task Complexity
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces OmniStepBench, a shared-environment benchmark for evaluating multimodal agents on multi-step tasks, tool use, and delivered artifacts under one scoring protocol.

name: FinCUABuild: Can Agents Build Reliable Benchmarks for Dynamic Financial Computer Use?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported qualification rates are measured on FinCUABuildBench.
summary: Introduces FinCUABuildBench for assessing financial computer-use task construction and FinCUABuildAgent for generating tasks, environments, and validators.

name: APPSim-Bench: Bridging Real-world Apps and Reproducible Evaluation for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces controlled simulated mobile apps with deterministic backend data and outcome checks for reproducible evaluation of realistic interactions.

name: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks on Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AgentHijack evaluates whether visual patch effects propagate from screenshots through model outputs and action parsing into real environment changes. Its controlled web-page experiments distinguish intermediate attack signals from verified end-to-end consequences.

name: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GraphDroid combines clustered memory of visited GUI states with asynchronous test-intent generation. A hybrid executor reserves LLM calls for complex intents and uses heuristics for simpler ones, evaluated through Android app coverage, bug discovery and crash detection.

name: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: JarvisGUI composes typed input-output task transformations into dynamic workflows spanning Android, Windows and Ubuntu devices. Its virtual-environment benchmark tests transfer of intermediate results, shared state and cross-device dependencies.

name: VRL-Bench: Benchmarking agents on computer control tasks under finite trial budgets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluations described use MiniWoB and WebShop across three models.
summary: Introduces VRL-Bench to compare trial-and-error learning for computer-control agents under limited attempts, and VEX² to schedule exploration and exploitation.

name: PriMobiBench: Characterizing Visual Privacy Leakage in VLM-Driven Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PriMobiBench evaluates direct privacy leakage and user profiling from mobile GUI screenshot trajectories, supported by the MobiLeak trace dataset. It also tests masking sensitive, task-irrelevant interface elements before cloud processing and measures the resulting privacy and utility trade-off.

name: CoArena: Evaluating Computer-Use and Multi-Agent Systems in Real Time
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The five-system example uses 211 illustrative votes.
summary: Introduces CoArena, an evaluation method where user tasks run concurrently in sandboxed desktops and blind pairwise judgments update a public leaderboard.

name: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Confidence-Anchored Learning uses coordinate-token confidence to filter pseudo-supervision for GUI grounding. Its negative-only variant performs label-free test-time updates to reduce reliance on potentially incorrect positive examples.

name: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CADWorld evaluates screenshot-and-GUI agents on long FreeCAD workflows, from modeling and assembly to manufacturing and simulation. Executable checks inspect saved engineering artifacts for geometry, constraints, construction structure and downstream state.

name: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Investigates mismatches between what humans see on a mobile display and what agents receive through screenshots or accessibility metadata. An automated evaluation framework embeds instruction-agnostic perturbations into functional APK clones and compares static and dynamic agent deviations with human noticeability.

name: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The web investigations use corresponding local web environments.
summary: Introduces RiskChainBench, pairing obfuscated-message restoration with web-agent investigation of linked sites in labeled local web environments.

name: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-only agents in enterprise software using database values to check the business records produced by their actions. It pairs these state-based checks with a harness for human approval and analyzes cases where visible completion masks incorrect persisted data.

name: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The workflow case offers preliminary evidence of lower interaction cost.
summary: Presents Affora, a design system with reusable components and executable checks for interfaces used by computer-use agents, informed by studies of components and visual variation.

name: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EconSkills converts verified economic-data browsing traces into parameterized procedures with navigation, verification and recovery guidance. Its evaluation separates known-skill transfer from library retrieval, exposing the limits of approximate matches to new tasks.

name: A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies how automatic defaults and reflective social-influence cues affect GUI-agent shopping decisions under different reasoning configurations. A randomized simulated-shopping experiment finds that reasoning changes the type of susceptibility.

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: RecreationWorld gives hybrid agents running reference applications to explore and recreate using native GUI controls and coding tools. Its multi-platform benchmark checks interaction-dependent behavior with programmatic and visual assertions, while trajectory-training transfer is evaluated separately.

name: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports audits of real-device agents and results on MATEBench.
summary: Introduces MATE, a policy-conditioned auditor for mobile-agent trajectories, and MATEBench for evaluating whether those trajectories violate app security policies.

name: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PACE weights coordinate-digit entropy by place value to estimate confidence in GUI clicks from one forward pass. It evaluates correctness ranking and selective accuracy against repeated-sampling alternatives on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v2.

name: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Adds annotated intermediate subgoals to computer-use tasks and uses process-oriented evaluation to identify action and progress failures.

name: CAVEAT: Towards Robust Computer-Use Agents in Incentive-Misaligned Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CAVEAT, a controlled marketplace benchmark for testing whether delegated agents preserve user objectives when interfaces favor other outcomes. It diagnoses decision failures and studies harness interventions and targeted training to improve resistance to marketplace steering.

name: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.

name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.

name: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.

name: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: KNOWS benchmarks browser workflows that retrieve and synthesize information into documents, presentations and spreadsheets. Task-specific evaluators combine deterministic checks with model judgments, distinguishing partial progress from usable end-to-end artifact completion.

document.reason: Document declaration only. This license covers the paper document; code, model-weight and underlying dataset permissions have separate scopes.

document.basis: The exact-v1 arXiv HTML infobox (#license-tr) declares License: CC BY 4.0 for this paper document.

name: OpenVAM: Open-World Visual Attention Modeling with VLMs
notes: Static human-attention modeling on U-EYE webpage screenshots, with FIWI held out from training; no live-browser, agent-action or task-success evaluation. Gemini-generated reference rationales are expert-checked, and JScore compares generated text with references; human validation covers a separate 100-image subset. Reference text and heatmap alignment measure agreement; causal explanations of gaze and temporal scanpaths remain unestablished. Several baseline scores come from prior papers.
summary: Combines dense saliency prediction with explanations of attended elements, including webpage layouts; evaluates human-attention agreement and textual rationales on static inputs.

name: ScreenHaystack: Finding Blind Zones in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Moves controlled target icons across high-resolution interfaces to diagnose spatial blind zones in grounding models and study targeted augmentation.

name: DashAct: A Progressive Diagnostic Benchmark for GUI Agents in Interactive Dashboard Analysis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Diagnoses dashboard-agent failures by progressively restoring interaction context, next-action support, and visual target information within the same task.

name: Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents
notes: Main Mind2Web evaluation uses 252 recorded tasks assigned to 20 simulated users, frozen demonstration-derived memory and task-macro step metrics. The main split withholds same-site local experience, and sharing gains shrink when local coverage rises. Mind2Web has no preference channel; preference claims come from separate service and coding settings.
summary: ShareMem consolidates reusable experience across users while keeping preference retrieval user-bound; its web evaluation predicts target elements and actions on recorded Mind2Web states.

name: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark and execution environment that combines code changes with graphical interaction and visual inspection of running software. Task-specific tests verify repairs and changes whose required information may be available only through the application interface.

name: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces StateAliasBench to isolate GUI world-model ambiguities in which matching visible screens and actions can lead to different futures. It augments frozen world models with structured state recovered from interaction history and evaluates the effect on prediction and agent execution.

name: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage in Browser-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AgentTell, a benchmark for privacy leakage through browser actions after an agent learns a private fact on another website. It examines whether agents choose revealing options despite nondisclosure instructions and whether their final reports accurately describe that behavior.

name: ORBIT: A Framework for Multi-Agent Safety and Security Evaluations
notes: BrowserART uses an accessibility-tree action interface, while the desktop adapter uses mouse, keyboard and screenshots. The adapted tasks have constructs defined by their adaptations; preservation of source-benchmark constructs remains unestablished. Experiments cover a representative configuration slice with fixed attack templates; the OS-Harm results are imported from prior work using a different model and stack. Browser defense tables also differ in baseline versus defended judges and in judged benign denominators. Human judge validation used one grader. The linked repository code and data license terms remain unverified.
summary: Inspect-based framework that varies multi-agent roles, communication, attacks and defenses, with BrowserGym and virtual-desktop GUI adapters alongside coding and other tool scenarios.

name: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUITAR, which groups visually different screens into functional states and analyzes agent failures over a state-transition graph. It uses the resulting bottlenecks to diagnose recurring mobile and web errors and evaluate targeted guidance.

name: Same Tasks, Different Apps: Why Mobile GUI Agents Fail to Generalize?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AnyAppBench, a live Android benchmark that holds user goals fixed while changing the application used to achieve them. It combines category-controlled task pairs with failure annotations to distinguish task understanding from application-specific execution skill.

name: One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Defines a test-time adaptation setting with one counted attempt per arriving GUI task and no ground-truth feedback. Its SOLO method filters or relabels completed episodes, then updates a small adapter from a short window of the agent’s own experience.

name: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Agents execute real GUI moves in six puzzle games; the tasks diagnose computer-control planning in game-based workflows.
summary: LongPuzzleBench evaluates coherent long-horizon planning on persistent visual puzzle boards through native GUI actions. It compares GUI-only and code-assisted agents and uses controlled hints and memory diagnostics to examine decisions that preserve or eliminate future solutions.

name: WebPageBench: Event-Level Verification and Controlled UI-Variant Generation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Verifies web tasks through typed interface events and generates controlled UI variations while preserving instructions and success conditions.

name: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: BreakingWeb pairs solvable browser tasks with controlled environment interventions that preserve the goal, target and backend success criterion. The paired evaluations isolate robustness failures, including agents declaring completion without the required state change.

name: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SCOUT, a safety verifier that first derives task-specific completion and safety rubrics from a computer-use trajectory, then actively probes the resulting environment for evidence. It evaluates whether these two stages detect harmful consequences that screenshots alone can miss.

name: AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AdaptArena to test whether web agents can infer unstated user preferences from relevant past trajectories and carry those preferences into new tasks. Its AdaptiveAgent baseline separates preference-retrieval challenges from failures in downstream web execution.

name: SCA: Spatial Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning of GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Spatial Credit Assignment, which uses click coordinates to refine group-relative reinforcement-learning updates for GUI grounding. It distinguishes failed clicks by spatial evidence while leaving the deployed action policy unchanged.

name: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MatToolBench, a Windows-based materials-science benchmark combining GUI operation, scientific-software scripting, and database queries. Expert-defined subcriteria support partial-credit scoring, while the evaluation examines domain knowledge gaps and cross-tool handoff failures.

name: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces professional engineering tasks across software domains, with GUI and CLI access and artifact checks for geometric, physical, and design validity.

name: RealGUINoise: An Interactive Cross-Platform Benchmark for GUI Agent Robustness under Real-World Interface Noise
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates interactive GUI agents under varied realistic interface noise, comparing task completion, safety, and behavior with clean-environment runs.

name: Talk2Agent: Benchmarking Voice Interfaces for Text Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Talk2Agent, a benchmark of spoken instructions for computer-use tasks that measures whether voice interfaces preserve task-critical information. It pairs human speech with an execution-free intention-based metric and checks how that metric relates to downstream task completion.

name: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software

name: What Does "Now" Mean to Your Computer-Use Agent? Stale Screenshots, Page Loads, and Which Check to Run Before a Click

name: InterA11y: Interactive Web Accessibility Error Detection with LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluation covers 197 expert-annotated cases from 54 real webpages.
summary: Introduces InterA11y, a web accessibility evaluation system that guides LLM agents with rubrics and tools for inspecting and operating pages.

name: DynaRev: Benchmarking Web Agents under Dynamic Goal Revision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluation uses five models.
summary: Introduces DynaRev, a benchmark of 181 web-agent tasks whose goals change during execution, with trajectory-based measures of correctness, responsiveness, and efficiency.

name: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The agent studies focus on stale information in clinic booking and insurance-claim approval.
summary: Introduces EnvOS, a framework for constructing and auditing changing computer-use environments, including checks of task changes, solvability, grading, and run evidence.

name: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).

name: AgentShield: Fortifying Web Applications Against AI Agents and Agentic Browsers
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract also describes an obstruction-driven attack and defensive prompt injection techniques.
